Question: Was Obi-Wan Kenobi an unfit master for Anakin Skywalker?
Answer: No, but he was not ideal, and that was unfortunately a big problem in his case. Obi-Wan was a perfect counterpart, but that alone was not enough. Anakin needed a perfect master, not just because he’s the Chosen One, but because of Sidious. The greatest evil mastermind and manipulator in the galaxy. If Palpatine wasn’t pulling string and messing up Anakin’s life, Obi-Wan would have served Anakin just fine. Skywalker was trained well and could handle intense pressure, just not Palpatine cranking it up to 12 So, Obi-Wan was fit for Anakin, but not for the full situation and the bigger picture of training the boy. A big reason Qui-Gon would have been better is that he could be a father. What Anakin needed, and what Palpatine ultimately filled in for. Kenobi could only be an older brother.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How do you view the dark side?
Answer: In the OT and Prequels, I love it. I always prefer the Light Side and heroes, all that stuff. More accurately a love to hate it… something like that. Just an evil perversion of the Force which is displayed through the Sith is amazing. I love the good vs evil theme, not good and evil. Selfish and power-hungry Sith is what I want to see in a villain. The old lore for both Sides is great. But in the new Canon, I’m not a huge fan. I don’t want a Dark Side that’s good in moderation, I want a Dark Side that is pure evil; the mixture can come from Sith or Jedi weak in either side, not strong in both. In the sequels Kylo was tempted by the Light Side and felt a pull to it, but still just wanted to stay on the Dark Side because. That’s something I don’t like at all, to put it lightly. A Dark Side that’s tempting is gold, one that baits with cookies or the like.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are the criteria for being a Jedi or Sith in the Star Wars universe? How do they differ from each other?
Answer: *During the prequel era* The only requirement is being part of either club. If you were part of the Jedi Order, you were a Jedi. And to be a Sith during this time, you had to be one of the two present Dark Lords! Only two true Sith can exist at a time during this period (and some others) And what separates them is… everything. They are opposites in almost everything outside of both wielding lightsabers and using the Force. Behold their codes: The Sith are selfish, the Jedi are selfless. One seeks to gain, one seeks to give. Classic “good vs evil” stuff. Although during TCW, lines can be blurred.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win, Kit Fisto Vs Obi-Wan Kenobi?
Answer: Kenobi would win. He outclasses Fisto in most regards. Even though Kit Fisto has shown to be quite impressive. It’s through few and otherwise basic feats. He beat Grievous, but to Kenobi? That’s cute. Obi-Wan is a far better duelist and no one’s Shii-Cho is piercing Kenobi’s Soresu if Anakin’s Djem So barely could. And in Force Power, Kit Fisto’s sadly shown nothing notable, while Obi-Wan is one of the strongest to ever cross the screen. He also sent Grievous flying (and he weighs 159 Kgs) Need I go on?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Tony Stark say to Peter Parker, “If you’re nothing without the suit, then you shouldn’t have it.”?
Answer: It’s what Peter needed to hear. Parker simply didn’t get that. He was enjoying the extra abilities the suit gave him. But not understanding what they are meant to do. We all know how the Super Soldier Serum works, right? The suits -Spidey’s and Stark’s - are just like that. They amplify what’s inside. Stark didn’t give the suit to a nobody; he gave it to level up a small-time/up-and-coming hero. Just like what he did for himself. He wanted to do good, on a larger scale, so he enabled himself to. But Peter wasn’t ready to be an Avenger. He still lacked experience, among other things. And it was way too dangerous at the time for Peter to be an Avenger (it always is, but not this much, and normally Avengers are adults who can make choices for themselves) And lastly, he couldn’t have all that extra power simply because of these wise words: “If you can do good things for other people, you have a moral obligation to do those things. It's not a choice; it's a responsibility.” - TASM’s Uncle Ben, inspired by Peter’s biological father If he had Avenger level power, he ought to be using it to fight Avenger level threats.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How big is a fully grown Rancor compared to a fully grown Krayt Dragon?
Answer: Comparatively, a Rancor is like a small snack for a Krayt Dragon. A Rancor is big… by human standards. (slightly exagerated) But a Krayt Dragon is massive compared to the Rancor. It’s almost a repeating ratio. 100 humans = 10 Rancor = 1 Krayt Dragon. It’s very rough, but you get the idea. Fully grown Krayts are way bigger than Rancor. The smallest of Krayt Dragons are probably bigger than the largest Rancor.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why couldn't Hela defeat Surtur?
Answer: Because her attacks did almost nothing to Surtur and he didn’t beat around the bush. Surtur just wanted Asgard gone, and that would take them both down. If he wanted to survive, then there would have been problems (it is possible neither would ever do sufficient damage to the other) Hela’s power on Asgard is incredible, and Surtur actually cannot die until he destroys the place. But we did not have to worry about that; as mentioned above, Surtur just wanted to destroy Asgard, and it is literally what he was born to do.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't Anakin Skywalker bleed to death when his legs were hacked off by Obi-Wan?
Answer: Burns, lightsabers prevent bleeding. But the reason Anakin did not die is because he held on to his life through a need for revenge and the Dark Side. The same way Maul survived being cut in half. It’s something a lot of people miss; they say Obi-Wan should have ended Anakin’s pain, but Anakin himself was fighting the end. Really, there is still an obvious argument to be made that Kenobi should have ended Anakin, but he did have to live to become Darth Vader.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Obi-Wan hate Maul for killing his master and Satine?
Answer: No. That’s one of the best things about the rivalry between Maul and Kenobi. Obi-Wan hated what Maul did, but knew that hate is what caused the damage in the first place, and that hating Maul wouldn’t help anyone. In the end, Maul died in Kenobi’s arms as if he was one of his own victims. Maul wanted to slowly cut up Kenobi, but Obi-Wan just did what he had to, and protect Luke. Nothing more; Obi-Wan even buried Maul and shared a conversation with him as if they were friends.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Spider-Man ever lose his powers in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU)?
Answer: No, he has yet to lose his powers. But I think it will be soon. Spider-Man has lost his powers for a brief period in a lot of adaptations. I’d bet if there will be two movies starring the character, he’d lose his powers in one of them. They pretty much reset him to be more like the OG comic Spider-Man, the setup is perfect, especially considering he loses his powers from emotional distress often (he’s in a pretty-very-extremely distressful situation) Otherwise, it could be thanks to a villain, but I’m sticking with emotional issues.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do you think it was strange for Obi-Wan to call Anakin "my old Padawan" instead of his name, especially in Revenge of the Sith?
Answer: Think about the difference. “My old Padawan” is not a name like “Anakin”. It’s a relationship between Obi-Wan and his… old Padawan. That’s special, only Obi-Wan can call Skywalker that (it wouldn’t make sense if it came from anyone else at least) It’s his version of “Ani” I guess. A term of endearment. Obi-Wan’s “old Padawan” has a special place in his heart, so I don’t think it’s weird. Anakin knew his master well, I’m sure he took it for what it was: a token of their special relationship.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How would a team-up between Obi-Wan and Batman go against Joker and Darth Vader?
Answer: Unfortunately, the villains win this one. Force Users are like speedsters: pretty OP and hard to fight if you’re not one of them. Joker and Batman don’t make much of a difference and the gap between Obi-wan and Vader is noticeable enough for most people to put their money on Vader. However, a team up isn’t just a 2v2. If Vader and Joker are on the same team, Joker would probably be the leader. And he’d orient the team. Obi-Wan and Batman are both strategic and might actually be able to neutralize the other team. A very interesting idea to me is Obi-Wan healing Joker’s broken mind. It could make for one good story. Batman, given preparation, could also make something to damage Darth Vader’s suit. If he could get it to affect Vader, Obi-Wan could beat the Sith, and we might just see ourselves a happy ending… sort of.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is a scene from a movie that made you unexpectedly tear up?
Answer: This one: Peter Parker mirroring his mentor, Tony Stark, in Spider-Man: Far from Home Iron Man was always my favorite character, so seeing the one character I thought worthy of being his successor was great. That’s what I thought when I watched it first at least. I was around 13 at the time. But thinking about it more, I think there’s a reason it hit oddly hard back then and still does: I’ve always related to Peter Parker a lot. Especially the MCU’s version, he’s like my MCU incarnate. And this scene is more than the passing of mantle, this is a young boy becoming his own hero. Becoming the man he never thought he could be as good as. And I could feel myself in that scene; I could imagine my older self rising to the high self-set bar. The dream come true; success in maturing and simply being able to look back later and think “I did it”. I was the person I always wanted to be. And that’s not fictional, that can happen, and I wish everyone could make it a reality in their own lives. I wish we can all grow up to know our younger selves would be proud.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If Qui-Gon Jinn had survived, how good of a general would he have been in The Clone Wars? Would he have survived Order 66?
Answer: Interesting scenario! I’ll have to go with a bad one. Because I don’t think he would have fought in the war at all. Qui-Gon was very intuitive, and possibly the best listener the Force has ever known. I believe he could have sensed the plot against the Jedi, had he been in the Clone Wars. While being an outcast for planting his feet on the other side of the council, I think he might have been able to reveal Sidious to the Jedi and save them. But hey, that’s just a theory… What’s yours?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are the three most emotional scenes in Star Wars?
Answer: This is completely subjective and based on my personal feelings watching the following scenes. 3: You Have Something - thrilling You can’t change my mind, this is the “I will find you” of Star Wars. Full body chills watching this. As Din came to rescue Grogu like how Gideon came to steal him, Djarin said exactly what the Moff did one season back. Verbatim. “You have something I want. You may think you have some idea of what you are in possession of, but you do not. In a few moments, it will be mine. It means more to me than you will ever know.” 2: Vader’s Redemption - amazement Obviously. This is the peak of Star Wars! THE moment of the SW universe. When the Chosen One fulfilled a prophecy everyone thought he never would. And the message of redemption is just so powerful. 1: Highground - utter misery “I hate you!” This is so emotional! The best of friends, closest of brother fighting to the death. All you could think of is the happy times and realize they’re gone and how it would feel to have someone like that in front of you, intending to kill you.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't Anakin's force ghost appear burned?
Answer: Because that’s not how the Force works! Your Force Ghost looks like your prime self… Possibly based on your physical prime, or maybe something else entirely. But one thing is for sure, Anakin’s ghost looking burned would be an inconsistency. Qui-Gon’s didn’t have a hole, so we know one’s old injuries do not appear. And Lucas felt the need to swap out Anakin’s Force Ghost from full adult to young adult. But even the old ghost did not have Anakin’s injuries: Arms, hair, no head wound. Yet Yoda and Obi-Wan are both still old. There is a difference though, that older Anakin never lived looking like that, it’s just what he would have looked like without the injuries. So, maybe it’s you healed body around the spiritual prime of your life? Let me hear your theory in the comments!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What was your least favorite episode of The Mandalorian and why? Do you think it could have been improved or should not have been aired at all?
Answer: Episode 6 in Season 3 O, celebrity guests… so un-Star Wars, so very Disney There was no rescuing it, this should not have aired. It’s the embodiment of every bad thing in Season 3. Just pure filler and laziness. Very unneeded. The Mandalorian’s earlier seasons barely wasted a second. But season three barely had relevant episodes. It honestly felt like a SpongeBob episode with Star Wars character. The only good parts of the episode just didn't belong and should have been saved for a better episode.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Qui-Gon Jinn discover immortality?
Answer: The details are still a matter of mystery, but it does make sense that he was led to it. He was concerned with an aspect of the Force no other Jedi was. The Cosmic Force. I hear a lot of people say Force Ghosts are part of the Living Force, but that’s not true. The Living Force is what the living Jedi are a part of. It flows through them and everything else. But the Cosmic Force is greater and what you become a part of when you die as a Light Sider. The Living Force is the Cosmic Force bound to and entering the living realm. And because of Qui-Gon’s connection to the Cosmic Force, he was most likely led to the Whills. It makes sense, since he guided Yoda to them. And they are Force Entities, so it would make sense they were born with the knowledge.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Was Palpatine afraid of Yoda before their fight during Order 66, or was he confident he would win their duel?
Answer: Oh, Palpatine was absolutely afraid. Remember this: Yoda saw it. This video kicks off right at this scene. Sidious is visibly scared and was trying to escape. And it really kicked off after Yoda’s Force Push. Palpatine felt his power firsthand, and it’s incredible. He was later disarmed by Yoda too, then he was really scared. Yoda and Sidious are very close in power and skill, Sidious was right to be afraid. All those years of planning were very close to being for nothing.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can you convince me that the Separatists were the good guys?
Answer: Probably not. Mostly because they were not the good guys! Separatist civilians were victims, but don’t let that fool you. The Separatists were led by Palpatine (Dooku was the figurehead and grievous lead he army) And they ultimately fought for the rise of the Empire and Order 66 Both big no-no’s if we’re talking net-good done. They’re methods of w4r were also just as bad as people claim the Republic’s were. (In reality worse; the droids terrorized billions of people and the CIS committed way more war cr1mes to living, feeling beings than the Republic did) The first season of the Clone Wars shows you the reality of it. Especially the liberation of Ryloth - the ending arc for S1

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What's a tiny detail you noticed in the Bad Batch?
Answer: Vantress uses the Light Side. Asajj using Animal Bond Before, she only used neutral or Dark Side abilities. Maybe I’m looking too far into it, but paring this -something that seemed to be set up as a big deal- up with her incredible reluctance to actually harm the Bat Batch makes me think she is actually dedicated to the Light Side now.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is a Darth?
Answer: A Sith Lord. Or should I say, a Dark Lord of the Sith? The word comes from squishing of the phrase. It’s for every member part of the Rule of Two. Any Master or Apprentice in the current duo. And some exceptions (but none in the Canon as far as I’m aware)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Asajj Ventress ever grow any hair on her head?
Answer: Yes. Most notably, in the Bad Batch. She’s got the ‘ol… okay this cut’s a bit new. That took some getting used to Even though she was seen with hair before, her appearance in the Bad Batch is probably her most popular out of the ones she has hair for.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do we really have to consider "The Bad Batch" Canon?
Answer: You don’t have to, but it is undeniably Canon. But why would you not want to? It’s great! A masterpiece with possibly the best animation Star Wars has seen. It’s like The Clone Wars part 2, but focusing on the CF-99 Yes, a step down from Obi-Wan, Anakin and Ahsoka, but fine in my opinion. We had a lot of that already, I like this new piece that’s from the old. The only part of it that conflicts with anything Canon is… nothing really. It just includes project necromancer, something sequels related. But it doesn't matter; take away the sequels and it still fits into the Canon fine, Palpatine’s plan just failed then.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can a double-sided lightsaber have two different coloured blades?
Answer: Yup. Think about Ventress’ lightsabers connecting. Both have their own Kyber, yet they can combine. So, it is absolutely possible to have to differently colored Kyber crystals in one double-lightsaber. But even standard doubles need two crystals, so you would not be sacrificing efficiency. In TPM (the first time a double was shown) we also see Maul’s hilt cut in half. Either he was lucky the one crystal was on the side Kenobi didn’t cut off, or there were two. Happy sabering!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Emperor Palpatine believe he was doing good for the galaxy?
Answer: Probably yes, but the actual net-effect he had on the galaxy was not a huge concern of his. Palpatine cared only for himself, he ruled because it meant he was in charge of all he could be in charge of. He also probably liked pretty much owning everything there is to own. Sith are naturally greedy. But let’s not forget he was a genius. He definitely tried to make sure people were hyper-controlled yet satisfied enough. To make his dream, “perfect”, long-lasting Empire. The incredibly small number of Rebels shows Sidious did a great job at scaring off people from rebelling while also providing enough to make living in utter submission a legit option subjects could see as the best option. He handled the galaxy quite well, but it turns out Star Wars has Captain America’s of its own, and people did want freedom.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are the reasons for the strong dislike towards the Separatists in the Star Wars franchise?
Answer: The only reason they’re “strongly disliked” would be because they are the “bad guys”, I assume. But they are not disliked. Ask any TCW fan, and you are likely to find the CIS is actually one of their favorite Star Wars factions. The droid army is hilarious, yet also daunting at times; but whenever, it is a very cool addition to a fan-favorite Star Wars era. If you mean inside the Star Wars universe, it’s simple: politics! The leaders of the Republic tried to get everyone hating the CIS and the CIS leaders tried to get all of their people hating the Republic.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How would MCU Thanos (Endgame) fare against pre-Stormbreaker Awakened Thor and Hulk (Age of Ultron) in a 1V2?
Answer: Not amazingly. Thanos could take down the Hulk and land hits on Thor. But that’s best-case. I do not see him winning. Thor is too fast and powerful. Look at that! Thanos is so cooked. Without Stones or anything other than a close-range Uru blade, Thanos has no chance against most versions of Thor.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What would happen if you could use the Force to crush the Kyber crystal in an opponent's lightsaber?
Answer: Nothing, because Jedi already can! Jedi do similar things. Namely, Ahsoka has turned off her opponent's lightsaber mid-fight. And saber throws rely on a similar technique. There’s a switch inside of most lightsaber which turns the blade off as it leaves its owner's hand. You can see the switch in action in most scenes where a lightsaber leaves a hand: So, we have established that Force users can mess with things inside lightsabers (their own and the opponent’s) But here’s why crushing the crystal would not happen. Kyber is tough, so is the rest of the hilt. It would take a lot of concentration, and when you’re dealing with Force Sensitives, split seconds count. Doing that mid-fight would likely give you a loss, and on top of this, you have to break your opponent’s Force Shield to mess with their lightsaber. Every wonder why Force Users don’t always yank each other’s sabers back and forth? Why they don’t toss each other around? Because of the Force Shield! It’s second nature to most Jedi; as the lightsaber ignites or fight starts, the Force Shield starts running. This is an ability that requires concentration, so it’s not always active. But for the most part, you’ll have to be a good bit stronger than an opponent to get past his or her Force Shield while it’s focused on.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win, Mace Windu vs Count Dooku?
Answer: Mace Windu. While I think they are both near equals in power and skill, Mace would win. Why? Because of Vaapad, that’s why! Makashi is not made for handling aggressive opponents (we see often how Anakin’s Djem So is problematic for Dooku) On top of that, Sith Lords are Vaapad’s specialty. Mace Windu cooks Dark Siders, which brings us to a valuable reference: Mace Windu out-dueled Palpatine: That’s someone far superior to Dooku. Considering a form advantage and this feat, I become quite confident Mace would win.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Count Dooku ever attempt to overthrow Sidious and become emperor?
Answer: Well, he did plan on taking out Sidious. But he never got around to that part. He was just a careful and smart man (so was Maul) All three were smart enough to see what was going on, and Palpatine’s intelligence in particular is what kept him a safe distance above his apprentices. Both Maul and Dooku looked for apprentices of their own to help overthrow Palpatine. Tryanus asked Kenobi to help, and probably meant to do the same with Asajj (but Palpatine sensed when she was becoming a threat) But if he did manage to overthrow Sidious, I’m not sure he would want to be emperor. Dooku wanted to rid the system of corruption, after taking out whoever he deemed corrupt, I doubt he’d want to stay in power. I think the Count would just set up his dream system… and see it fall.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the lightsaber form that Darth Maul uses? Is he considered as a great duelist in Star Wars?
Answer: Firstly, I’ll say he is a great duelist. As for being considered one, that’s debatable. He is not one that comes to mind for most people, but I’d say he’s definitely worthy of being called a great duelist. As for his form, it’s Juyo (and Niman, but that’s because the form is adaptable for his double-lightsaber and incorporates other weapons like the Force and one’s own limbs) It is ferocious and wild; strong, aggressive and tied to feelings. Maul is reactive and can be defensive, but his strength lies in unpredictable and uncontained offense.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't Stark let Bucky snap? I mean he has a metal arm.
Answer: Metal arms don’t quite cut it with the Infinity Stones. I’d argue Tony’s suit would do a better job at protecting than Bucky’s arm, but regardless, neither could prevent death. I’m not sure if anything shown in the MCU can save a human from the power of the stones. Hulk was hurt with the specialized Nano-Gauntlet, which multiple geniuses worked on (including Rocket, who is well-versed with the stones) The only time someone snapped without being seriously harmed was this time: And Thanos had an Asgardian gauntlet with magical elements on top of his Titan-ness. So, I really doubt Bucky could survive. Plus, he was a very minor character; it would have been a bad choice from a directing perspective.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Has a Jedi ever wielded a red lightsaber despite not being a Sith?
Answer: Absolutely. In Canon, there are many instances of Jedi using a Sith’s blade for a limited time. But in Legends, some Jedi own red lightsabers. Most notably, Adi-Gallia. In there, red was a natural color for Kyber. But Jedi would only wield red blades when Sith weren’t around for obvious reasons.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How stupid were the Jedi that they never knew that Palpatine was playing both sides? Come on, even a clone found out…
Answer: Not that stupid actually. Obi-Wan was the only Jedi who was a little dumb concerning the grand matter of Palpatine’s orchestration. Dooku told him too much but got lucky. Other than that scene in AotC, you must realize the Jedi did not get as much as we did. They weren’t even sure Maul was the apprentice (Dooku was the Sith Lord almost certainly if you look at evidence; Palpatine did a great job at hiding in plain sight and cleaning up tracks) Jedi did not have the information we had as viewers, it’s not even remotely close. I find it very understandable how the Jedi did not find Palpatine out. And that was one clone out of billions, who had the Emperor reveal himself.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What does Yoda represent?
Answer: The guide. He is the person that guides the hero. And we all have one in our lives, so this role is incredibly powerful. Yoda is a source of wisdom, one powerful, but ready to help the learner surpass. They’re usually good with people, patient and compatible with any student (showing off the years of living and all that) It’s quite simple. He’s like the Uncle Iroh/Uncle Ben of Star Wars. Outside of the OT, he’s less relevant to our lives. In the prequels Yoda is a representation of the Jedi Order’s peak then and there. “The most powerful and wise, best of the best” Very cool, but less art-like.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What makes 'The Mandalorian' popular among Star Wars fans, but disliked by critics?
Answer: I think you should be asking “why don’t Star Wars fans like the Mandalorian as much as critics?” Avg. score is from the combined ratings of each season, both 1 and 2 have a 93% critic score I think what makes it popular among both is simply the quality. It is a really good show. The music, action, slower scenes, dialogue, plot, visuals and acting are all fantastic! (Until S3 of course) And I think the critics appreciate it more because of that combined with the fact a few fans probably don’t like it simply for how there aren't many Jedi in. Personally, its light detachment from Star Wars is part of the appeal. Overall, I’d say only season three is actually disliked.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the rarest type of lightsaber color? Who has used it (not including force wielders)?
Answer: Pink! In Canon, Cal can have any color + some unique to the game. Now maybe this doesn't officially add it to the Canon, but I was going for a rebellious answer anyway. With that said, the most obvious answers may be the best: purple/orange But one part of the question gives what I think of as the actual best answer! Who has used it (not including force wielders)? There’s only one that could come to mind: The Darksaber is a totally unique lightsaber and has actually only been wielded by two Force users ever! (The Jedi-Mandalorian creator and Darth Maul) The Darksaber is the only black saber and is wielded by a Mandalorian (non-Force-sensitive) at almost every moment. So, there it is.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why is Rey given the Skywalker surname in Rise Of Skywalker, despite the fact that she wasn't said to be related to Luke at all, in The Last Jedi ?
Answer: She was not given the name, she called herself that. People absolutely hate it. Although, I must be honest, I don’t really mind. Okay okay okay, I get it, the other Skywalkers are way better, fine. But putting aside how it was received, you’ll see it was meant to be about choosing family. Rey is not like Sidious, at heart, she’s no Palpatine. And in the films, she is meant to be a hero, like the Skywalkers. I don’t love the movies, but I think this whole “Rey Skywalker” thing is unfairly critiqued. Luke and Leia were more like parents to her than her actual ones ever were. I’m okay with the name.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are the most powerful types of lightsabers? Is there anything more powerful than Kyber crystals?
Answer: Not really in terms of what’s Canon. However, there are some special types of crystals in Legends. To be honest, I find them silly and goofy. There’s a lava saber that spews lava out pretty much magically. There’s an acid Kyber, a poison one, etcetera. All with “video-game powers” and that kind of stuff. Other than the Kyber crystals, there are some types of lightsabers that use normal Kyber and seem advantageous:

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Marvel reluctant to create new superheroes for people to idolize and admire like their old ones?
Answer: Wha- no, not even remotely! Marvel’s leaning into new characters pretty hard. Ironheart, Shuri, She-Hulk, Sam, Khan, Kate Bishop. Some misses, some hits. Some are old, getting spotlight; some a new coming in for the first time. And if you’re talking about comics… not quite. Old ones are what sell; resetting the multiverse and making a new version is like a cheat code. It works really well, so, it’s just business. Sadly, if you’re looking for new characters, Marvel probably won’t give much because any new character has very little chance of becoming as profitable and popualr as the old.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What if Darth Maul was a Jedi?
Answer: We would have one very interesting Jedi. Design wise, he’s always been one of the coolest characters ever. I imagine he’d still have the double saber. Fun fact: Maul was actually blue with gold hints - like Chuchi - in the original concept art And probably keep an all-round mean look. Which is something I like for Jedi, it’s a reminder about not judging people. Although, this would be a totally new character. Maul represents the Sith very well. Everything about him is perfectly Sith. Only Palpatine beats him in terms of being an ideal Sith (of Canon Sith) I really cannot see him being a Jedi. Although keeping his Midi-Count, I can be pretty sure he’d be a powerful fan-favourite thanks to that and appearance.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can you provide examples of powerful villains who cannot be defeated by heroes, but can be easily defeated by other villains?
Answer: Does this guy count? Not really. And the examples are very few and far between because it makes for a bad story most of the time. If no hero can stand up to the villains of a universe, it’s just a dark dystopian piece. Not inspiring, no relatable arc, no classic structure.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Anakin use the force to win the pod race?
Answer: Yup, and he’s done it before. The Force and some abilities very often become second nature to Jedi. But Anakin was special, he had more potential than anyone in the history of Star Wars. So, the most basic ability of the Force (sensing/heightened reaction) came naturally even without training. The only human in the Star Wars Canon known to race pods Anakin was not consciously using the Force, but it was with him and giving him a very heightened reaction speed.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Was it ever demonstrated how much stronger Anakin was compared to Obi-Wan during their fight on Mustafar?
Answer: Yes, behold: Anakin’s prime is far, far greater than Kenobi’s. But during the duel, they were even. In Force power, it was a near tie, same for skill. Anakin just came from doing a lot of “the unthinkable”. So, he was not in ship-shape as far as Vader goes. While Obi-Wan was in his absolute peak, that is for sure. The fight was his to win. Anakin and Obi-Wan have almost always stayed somewhat relative to each other. Implying Anakin was way more powerful during the time is… obviously false. The creators of Star Wars gave us the direct pretty comparison, and it’s also the original. Feats and statements that suggest otherwise would be inconsistencies; but you’re free to have whatever opinion you want, this is just mine. Have a great day!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win in a fight between Asajj Ventress and the adult Ahsoka Tano?
Answer: Ahsoka. She could compete with Vader as an adult. Ventress simply has nothing on that. And while I’d say Asajj was above Ahsoka during TCW, after it’s pretty visibly false. Tano just surpassed Ventress through faster growth. Unless Bad Batch Ventress was training hard and just didn’t get the chance to show off, I don’t think any version of her can beat Rebels Tano. If we’re talking about Ahsoka from her own series, I think the answer stays the same. Nothing truly suggested Ahsoka fell off or anything.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did the creators of Spiderverse choose to have a different person as Spider-Man? Was it for diversity reasons or were there other factors involved?
Answer: One of the main points of the film was that anyone could wear the mask. Having the old Spidey we know and love as the main character would not help sell the point nearly as well. And the plot revolves around Spider-Man’s successor taking up the great responsibility. It was to tell a new and different story (a freaking great one too) So, not only were there other factors involved, but I think the “diversity thing” was not even one minor factor. (Gwen: white, Parkers: both white, Peni: white etc. They didn’t focus on that nonsense; they just made a good film)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Hawkeye return after being blipped out? Was he not snapped out with any other Avengers like Iron Man or Captain Marvel?
Answer: He was, indeed, safe from the snap. Clint Barton was not on of the people who were taken by the blip, but his entire family was. So, understandably, after that, he went on to fight crime Batman style. But without the no-kill-rule. The brutal Ronin was born. And he was killing criminals at large for a lot of those 5 years.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: *Spoiler* at the end of Spider-Man: No Way Home, why did Peter decide to not introduce himself to MJ and Ned or remind them of their previous relationships?
Answer: Picture the scene again. Peter walks to the place MJ works at. He sees Ned there too; he walks up to start conversation and keep his promise. But then… Something catches his attention. He sees what little is left of an injury MJ picked up during the intense battles of the movie. And he realizes he puts her in danger. Maybe not for the first time, but he’s focused on it now. Does he really want to drag her back into the mess? It’s not an easy life for her, and not very safe either. So, out of his love for her, he leaves without saying anything to either of his friends. To protect them.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which is more powerful, a lightsaber or an Infinity stone?
Answer: An Infinity Stone, by far. Lightsabers are common weapons in Star Wars, but the Infinity Stones are the most powerful things in the MCU (which easily scales higher at Canon peaks) Infinity Stones can kill mortals that try using their power. Those things need magical, often Asgardian, artifacts for scientific marvels just to contain their power. Lightsabers just need some metal case. So, power easily goes to the stones. However, don’t buy either at your local store unless you’re a skilled Jedi or cosmic titan of some kind; they’re both very dangerous.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why do you think Ahsoka was so cold and distinct from Anakin in season 7?
Answer: Unfortunately, it just was not the time to be touchy-feely. Mandalore was in defining moments. And Ahsoka has a job to do. Plus, to be fair, she was not that cold. As much as Tano didn’t want to get all involved and what-not, she shared a nice moment with Anakin. She didn’t feel like explaining her choices while people died or taking up debate with the Jedi and her own new views while people died. And the best part is Skywalker knew. He didn’t ask anything of Ahsoka, he simply gave her a warm welcome and two blue, better-than-new lightsabers.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Yoda have any other fears besides Palpatine?
Answer: Not any I can think of; Yoda was built different; he doesn't get scared easily. In fact, I am pretty sure Yoda had no fear of Palpatine. Yoda valiantly fought the Sith Lord. And was in constant pursuit of him. Fear was no Yoda’s weakness, he was very brave. Yoda’s real weakness lied in a “foolish bravery”. He ended up acting like the Jedi were invincible, he only began to take the needed actions when it was far too late. Yoda obsessed over Palpatine partly because he didn’t think there was anything else to worry about other than ending the Sith and Clone War. Remember things Yoda did, like hiding the fact that their enemies made the clones? Yoda was arrogant in this way, just as Sidious said. He had no idea the Jedi were stepping closer to extinction each day they fought.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What's something only a true fan will recognize?
Answer: MCU: A little something special we saw in the first MCU movie ever was floating down the river during Tony’s funeral. Star Wars: Maul’s moves were the exact same in this duel as the moves in TPM (the ones that killed Qui-Gon)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Anakin Skywalker dumb? He seems to make a lot of stupid decisions in the prequels.
Answer: No, not at all. Anakin is a genius. A tactician beyond brilliant and mechanical wizard! He made C3-P0 from scratch by the age of 10 with limited parts. Mostly. And he’s proved time and time again he’s an amazing strategist. He’s shown making dumb decisions because he let his emotions control him. Anakin knew what he should have done, but just could not bring himself to overcome feelings of fear and desire. The Prequels focus on Anakin’s fall, he’s constantly going through a lot there; other projects better show his actual intelligence. His poor choices were due to lack of maturity in the emotion-control department.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How is it that you're so wise?
Answer: I think I was born wise. To be honest, I’m sure I looked like this as a baby: Ok, serious answer: I’m not going to say I’m wise, but analytically, I think this is how one would become wise: By always thinking and questioning, passionately striving for wisdom And the person should truly value wisdom. Not just that, but wisdom should be their compass for value. That’s why wisdom is so important (more so than intelligence, I’ll add; I know a lot of fellow INTJs prefer intelligence, but I must say it’s just not important in comparison) A wise person will also share discovered truth. If you gain some understanding that was difficult to find, you will absolutely want to share it. And the easiest way is to learn from ones who are already wise. I could go on, but I honestly considered having this just be a meme answer, so, I hope this was satisfactory. Bye!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't Anakin's Force ghost appear to Kylo Ren in the Star Wars sequel trilogy?
Answer: Outside of the universe, it’s because it didn’t work with what directors wanted. But it actually makes sense in-universe. Force Ghosts do not work anything like most people think they do. Let’s look at some other instances of Force Ghosts appearing and speaking: “I was always there, Obi-Wan, you just weren't ready to see me.” Obi-Wan knew Qui-Gon well, and he did not see Jinn for quite some time. (Obi-Wan has already been on Tatooine for a while before the series takes off) Kylo Ren was not trying to see Anakin, and Skywalker was not trying as hard as Qui-Gon either. And if Kenobi was not ready to see his old master, there is no way Ren was ready to see his grandfather. Yoda was a legendary Jedi and arguable the most powerful Jedi to ever live (only in the Canon, maybe excluding Luke) And when Qui-Gon managed to communicate with Yoda (who has likely fully developed in the mysterious ways relevant to communing with Force Ghosts) he actually doubted himself. Yoda himself was unsure, so, I must say it’s completely sensible that Kylo could not communicate with Anakin.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How many Jedi and Sith were there in the Star Wars universe? Why was there a significant difference in their numbers?
Answer: During the Clone Wars/ the Prequel era there were about 20,000 Jedi, I believe. And for the Sith, about the same, just divided by about 10,000. Yeah, the Sith follow something called the Rule of Two. It was established long before TPM and goes on and off because some Sith don’t believe in the tradition. At any given moment, there should be one master and one apprentice. No more, no less. Sith don’t work together very well, but this rule forces them to. Why is that beneficial? The main reason is knowledge. If a Sith dies alone, all his or her knowledge goes out too. Because of the rule, each generation of Sith gets stronger than the last (that’s the idea at least) And the Jedi, on the other hand, needed no such rule. They work together just fine, and unlike the Sith, Jedi like to share. That is why there’s a big difference in their numbers.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If Darth Vader encountered Asajj Ventress, could he take her as his Sith apprentice and destroy Emperor Palpatine together with her?
Answer: He could try, but it would not end up working. Firstly, because Palpatine would be waiting for betrayal, he always has been, always will be. Paranoia is in Sith nature. But we also have to consider Ventress agreeing. I personally don’t think Bad Batch Asajj would accept the offer. She seems to be done with that galaxy-wide conflict thing. And actually, being an assassin in general. Sure, she still hunts, but I think she grew tired of killing.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What led Luke to believe that Vader was evil?
Answer: I mean, Vader doesn’t exactly look like a teddy bear… And his actions don’t prove him kind either. Darth Vader’s pretty dang evil; Luke had every right to think so. The Sith Lord tears through Rebels for fun and earned the name youngling wreaker for… I think you could guess. The real question is how did Luke see the good in Vader. And that’s up to debate in my opinion. Personally, I think it’s in Luke’s personality, what do you think?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is it possible that Darth Vader lost much of his potential power to eventually surpass the emperor during his fight and loss to Obi-Wan?
Answer: Possible? That’s exactly what happened! (Old Canon) According to George Lucas, Vader was 80% of what Palpatine was. Four fifths as powerful; and he could have been twice as powerful if he reached his full potential. But that was impossible in the G-Canon, because Anakin did, in fact, lose potential along with his limbs. And as much as I am a fan of Lucas and the older Canon, I do think it makes more sense to have your M-Count determine your Force potential rather than actual amount of Midi-Chlorians total. Because it doesn’t add up with little ones like Grogu, and it would also mean simply getting fat would increase your Force power.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Are Darth Vader and Anakin Skywalker truly the same?
Answer: It’s a matter of debate in the fandom, but I think here’s a good example: Are Spider-Man and Peter Parker the same? Logically, yes. Anakin just calls himself Vader after RotS, and so do others; it’s just a new name. But artistically, emotionally, not quite. (I’ll write as if the identities are two separate people here on) They act different, they look different… and talk differently. Vader is a Sith, Anakin is a Jedi. One’s a hero with extreme charisma, the other is a villain devoid of personality (mostly) Just like how Spider-Man is confident while Parker is nerdier.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can you list the most iconic scenes from each Star Wars movie in chronological order of release?
Answer: Episode IV’s moment: The First Scene! Darth Vader’s entrance, the Imperial March. Episode V’s moment: This is probably the most iconic scene of all Star Wars. Episode VI’s moment: Tight one between this and the actual scene where Vader betrays Palpatine. Episode I’s moment: You can do that??? The duel was next level, no disagreesies. Episode II’s moment: I’m not too sure here, but this is probably the most popular among fans. Episode III’s moment: Now, onto the sequels (ones that did not really age, so, these aren't super iconic) Episode VII’s moment: Snowy duel, this moment is quite famous. And the scene that gave the most iconic feel was here - Rey pulling the lightsaber to her. Episode VIII’s moment: Another wobbly one, it’s between Luke’s projection, Snoke’s death and the proceeding fight, Ben’s death, and the soaking duel. Episode IX’s moment: It’s by far the most memorable. And the climax of the entire trilogy: Palpatine dies again!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is it possible to use a vibroblade in a similar way to a lightsaber?
Answer: Not really. They’re just too different. Vibroswords: You can’t move it like a lightsaber, and even if you could, it wouldn’t cut through nearly as much. A lose for Vibroswords Those weapons are best for stabbing and maybe slicing sometimes. Lightsabers are for crazy space wizards swinging them around in every direction at Mach 3

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In Star Wars, does Qui-Gon Jinn ever come back from the dead to return to life?
Answer: Of course not! Let’s look at why: For starters, he’s not really all that dead. Qui-Gon achieved immortality, he’s more alive than ever. That leads us to point two: he does not want to get a body again. Being a Force Ghost is cool; it’s calm. Jinn likes it there, it’s where he belongs. And the final point is that coming back to life/a body wouldn’t really make sense. Not to me at least. It’s just a strange thing to think up, “ghosts” are associated with immortality and being unbound by space and time. And there’s zero need for it; Force Ghosts can already manifest themselves if they want to interact with the living.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is stronger, Luke or Anakin in their prime? Why does everyone say Anakin was more powerful when they had an equal amount of power and training?
Answer: I can’t remember anyone saying they had equal power and training, and I can assure you that’s not true. Anakin had far more training, it was just much easier. Luke fought Vader early on, but Anakin was not offered true challenges often enough grow to his potential. He rose to extreme power quickly, but did not push himself often, not like Luke. And who would win in prime forms depends on what prime means here. If it means we use the strongest version of Luke and the strongest version of Anakin, I’d say Luke. (Excluding Force Ghost Anakin) Luke reached more of his potential than Anakin did his own, and their M-counts are very similar. So, that’s my take, hope it helps!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Luke choose to search for Yoda instead of Obi-Wan?
Answer: What? That was not an option. Firstly, Obi-Wan came to Luke; Skywalker was not searching for anyone before Obi-Wan came along. Secondly: Luke searched for Yoda because Obi-Wan told him to! Luke did not choose between the two; Obi-Wan came to Luke, then led him to Yoda.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are some annoying misconceptions about your favorite superhero/heroes?
Answer: “IRON MAN is nothing without his suit” Honestly, I find the claim ridiculous. IRON MAN 3 was about proving how much more Tony Stark is IRON MAN than some suit. Harley Keener: “Is that Iron Man?” Tony: “Technically I am.” The suit enables Tony to actually fight Titans, Asgardians, etc. He even says to Peter, “If you’re nothing without the suit, then you shouldn't have it.” Stark absolutely lives by those rules. His genius and bravery make him a hero, the sui just lets him be a hero that can fight greater threats. And, of course, he’s still a billionaire, genius, playboy, philanthropist.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did you like the role of Anakin Skywalker?
Answer: No, no, no; I loved it. Anakin’s role is what makes Star Wars! Now, I don’t relate to him, and he’s not a big favorite of mine. But if there is one main character of Star Wars, it’s the Chosen One. As the title implies. He is brought up as a great Jedi, legendary guardian. He protects, gets manipulated, then falls. He destroys, becomes a monster. Until finally, he is redeemed, and brings balance to the Force by destroying the Sith, That is the main story of Star Wars. Episodes 1–6 To me, saying you don’t like the role of Anakin is to say you don’t like most of SW, more so just bits of it.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What’s with SW fans & calling Order 66 ‘The Fall of the Jedi’, instead of what it was—a horrific genocide? Are fans allergic to the word? Or just believe they ‘deserve what they got’?
Answer: When a fan mentions the fall of the Jedi, they normally aren’t just referring to Order 66. Rather, they are referring to the period leading up to that. It was the fall of the Jedi, to be honest. And it’s a part of Star Wars history and the end of a period. Just like in actual history we refer to the rise and fall of empires, kingdoms, etc. However, it was horrific genocide in universe. And some fans to think the Jedi got what they deserved with that. What Order 66 really was Probably just to be different and get some attention; it often seems like these fans think they’ve unlocked secret knowledge no one else considered and was blind to.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't the Jedi Council promote Anakin after he defeated Dooku?
Answer: Defeating a Sith will not get you promoted (by itself) This may be confusing as Anakin was promoted for losing to Dooku. But apparently, the last trial holding him back from being a Knight was the trial of flesh. Which he was argued to have passed when Dooku cut off an arm. As for why Anakin was not made master for winning: The rank was not given for outstanding bravery or skill or power. It was given for understanding, patience, knowledge, etcetera. Anakin never fully developed to round out his impatience and character flaws. The Council saw Skywalker just lacked the wisdom to be a master. Although we do have this…

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Will Miguel O'Hara have a similar fate to Anakin in Beyond? That is, humiliated, alone, and transformed into a monster without humanity?
Answer: This sounds like an indirect, yet effective, way to tell someone you don’t know Anakin or ATSV’s Miguel. Firstly, Anakin’s fate was redemption. The “monster” turned out to still have a Jedi inside. And it only took Luke’s faith to make that monster the great Hero of Star Wars. Secondly, no. Spider-Man 2099 will not meet any sort of end like Anakin’s defeat in RotS. He isn’t even bad. Just hardened by trauma (his character us really well-done, I must say) I think he’ll actually end up on Miles’ side. But even if he doesn’t, he’d probably go out in a heroic way. He’s not been set up as a villain, he’s been set up as a complex character that’s fighting for the lesser of two evils too passionately. And in a way the makes you feel for the poor guy.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why do Yoda and Obi-Wan disappear when they die yet other Jedi do not?
Answer: Because it’s not something all Jedi do, it’s a unique and very rare skill. The skill was discovered by Qui-Gon Jinn (Canon) And in the afterlife, Qui-Gon lead Yoda to discover the power. Yoda followed Qui-Gon’s instructions and that lead to these: the Whills Very mysterious Force entities. They taught Yoda the actual power of Jedi Immortality A.K.A. the Force Ghost ability. And then after that - at the end of Revenge of the Sith - Yoda tell Obi-Wan of Qui-Gon’s discovery and then Kenobi goes on to learn from Jinn too.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do you think it would've been cool if Yaddle, the female from Yoda's species, spoke like Yoda?
Answer: I actually prefer her speaking normally. Yaddle’s normal speech (which is somewhat clipped actually) adds even more mystery to Yoda and the species. They don’t have any set way to speak, no known home planet; we really have very little to go on. And I really like it. On another plus side, it differentiates Yaddle from Yoda, making her more of a sperate character than just a “girl Yoda”. I’d like to see more of her in Canon, she has a lot of potential and in Legends they did a great job at making her unique.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Obi-Wan ever fight Anakin after the latter turned into Darth Vader?
Answer: Yes, thrice in the Canon. Assuming we are not counting the duel on Mustafar. Anakin was already called Darth Vader at that point, but it’s often overlooked. The 3rd (chronologically) is the first lightsaber duel ever to come on the big screen! And the other two are from the Kenobi series. In the show, their first encounter goes as you would expect. The actual Darth Vader vs out-of-practice Obi-Wan. Obi-Wan gets absolutely destroyed; dragged around and everything. But the next… was controversial. Very much so. Vader walks away thinking he won while Obi-Wan is in a pit, buried by rocks. But Kenobi thinks about what purpose he still has, his reason to live. He lets go of his guilt and becomes the perfect conduit for the Force itself to flow through. That or plot malarkey. You can decide.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do you think Plo Koon is a B-tier Jedi?
Answer: If A is reserved for Sidious, Yoda, and the like, yes. Otherwise, heck no. Plo Koon is an A-tier. And if this list isn’t just based on power and skill, he’s S. Easily one of the top 3 Jedi to ever live! Firstly, let’s tackle skill and power: (Canon) Plo Koon could blitz Aurra Sing, use many Force attacks in quick secession, sense and communicate with Ahsoka through space and much, much more (with 30 mins of screentime, most of which includes him being in the background) And in Legends he could beat Ventress while he had a broken arm (as a practitioner of Form V) As well as communicate halfway across the galaxy. Back to Canon, he’s also compared to Mace Windu by Maul (an expert on the Jedi after years of observation) Now, for things outside of power: Plo Koon has a heart of gold! One of the most pure in all of Star Wars. He provides encouragement and love to all his troopers (which many Jedi do not even recognize as sentient) And they love him back, they spray paint “Plo’s Bros” on their ships and share a tight relationship with the rest of the Wolf Pack. Plo Koon is very humble and cares for all life; he provides help and teaching whenever he can, like when he provided comfort to Anakin during Ahsoka’s capture by Trandoshans. Not to mention his knowledge and wisdom go very deep.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Obi-Wan change his name to Ben while exiled on Tatooine?
Answer: In Canon, just for the reasons you’d think. It sounds like his real name, and he had to leave his actual one behind to stay hidden. In Legends, the reason he chose “Ben” specifically is because Satine called him that. So, it brought him some peace and it’s a name he would answer to naturally. And in case you wonder why he kept the surname “Kenobi”: He meant to leave it. But a young girl snoops around at night and eavesdrops outside Kenobi’s hut while he talks to Qui-Gon out loud. He doesn’t even know if Qui-Gon hears anything at that point but switches back to talking in thoughts after he learns about how talking aloud cost him privacy. And ironically, there are many Kenobi’s on Tatooine. This was given when the girl and some diners have a discussion trying to figure out which family he’s from with the new information.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Luke become a Jedi? Did Leia know she was a Jedi?
Answer: I’m going to mix the question up a bit just to set something straight first. Did Leia know she was a Jedi? When she was a Jedi, she did. A Jedi is a title for being part of an order. Like a member of a club. But speaking of Force-Sensitivity, she did not know she was Force Sensitive for a long time. Even by Return of the Jedi, I’m fairly certain she did not understand much of the Force. So, somewhere after RotJ where Luke began training Leia is when she understood Force Sensitivity, and she knew she had it a little earlier. Probably, she knew there was something special about her in that sense even earlier. How did Luke become a Jedi? Luke became one when he accepted training from Old Ben. Once he was told of his potential, and reached the point of no return (the death of his guardians) He set to becoming a Jedi. Then and there, he became a Jedi (a very new leaner, but a Jedi) Luke became a Jedi Knight once he faced his fear and confronted Vader. Yoda told him when he did that, he would be a Jedi Knight. Even though Luke was more powerful than almost any Jedi before him, he needed to show bravery, face his fear that was the last chain holding him back from being a fully developed hero. And he didn’t just fight Vader, he proved to be one of the greats by sparing him.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why couldn't Obi-Wan Kenobi sense the good in Darth Vader that Luke did?
Answer: A few reasons. Kenobi had few opportunities to sense anything on Vader. And the few instances where it was possible, the two were in a high-stakes duel. A lot of people think he was, but it’s just a cover up for Obi-Wan beating Vader. (Vader is obviously the more powerful, but he does not lose thanks to confliction) In the series, Obi-Wan was a perfect conduit for the Force; and Vader only really felt conflicted after Obi-Wan’s death, because one of the largest parts of Darth’s life was finally gone. But Luke was the last bit of Padme left in the galaxy (him and Leia) Luke was someone who believed, then looked in Vader for good. And then Vader was truly conflicted, barely attacking Luke, looking confused all the time. By the time Vader was truly coming back to the Light, Obi-Wan had seen too much destruction and misery. For anyone in the Star Wars universe, it would make sense to not see a possibility for redemption. Vader has done many, many horrible things. You can’t really blame someone for not thinking the Sith Lord could come back. Obi-Wan like most others saw no trace of the old Anakin left in Vader.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What's something you look forward to seeing more of in the MCU?
Answer: I’m looking forward to seeing more origin stories scaled back a bit. (Obviously I also would like more of the old quality) Thanos was great but mostly because of his great build up. We don’t need world-ending threats every movie. Street level heroes like Spider-Man do just fine. Speaking of which, Spider-Man’s next step is what I’m excited for most in the MCU.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How do I make an MCU fan mad?
Answer: * DCEU Supes solos the MCU * Thanos isn’t that powerful, Steppy beats him mid-diff. * The MCU’s been getting progressively better (best series is She-Hulk), but GotG 3 was a fail.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What ever happened to the 104th after order 66?
Answer: We don’t know. All we see is that the 104th seems to have joined the Empire like any other squad at first. However, Wolffe does slowly overcome his programing. The commander lets Rex and the boys go free, and a long time later he ends up as one of the three clones on the Void. So, I assume he escaped the Empire, but the rest of the Wolf Pack very possibly went on with generic lives.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who’s your least and most favorite powerscaler?
Answer: Least favorite, I’m not going to name anyone. Just a type of scaler can annoy me at times. Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is considered to have the strongest lightsaber? Is there a difference if both users have equally strong ones?
Answer: Generally, if the average fan had to pick, it would be whoever wields the Darksaber. Because that’s one of the only unique lightsabers. Almost every lightsaber is the same except for color. You get types like the double lightsaber and shoto sabers, but they are still fundamentally the same. And then we have exceptions… In Legends, there are other types lightsabers/kyber crystals. To be honest, I think they are very dumb ideas, but here’s an example anyway: Lava Lightsabers These would spew lava at the opponent in combat. How? Why? I don’t want to know, but it’s a thing and definitely advantageous.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What would happen if the dark side of the force was destroyed?
Answer: The Sides aren't constants. So, nothing cataclysmic. The Dark Side being destroyed would just mean no one is abusing the Force. But the potential would always be there. Sooner or later, someone will come a long and decide “stuff the Light Side, how about my way/more power etc.?”

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Are you excited for a Wookiee Jedi in "The Acolyte"?
Answer: We’ve already had three. (Maybe 4 and I just don't know about the other) Tyvokka, Gungi and an initiate from the Yoda comics. And since general reception of the show is negative, I must say I am not. Tyvokka, Plo Koon’s master and former Council member. I honestly didn’t have high hopes for the Acolyte, and based on reviews I have read (positive and negative) it seems the shows is not meeting my expectations. Although Wookie Jedi are always fun to see, and seeing one in live-action could be cool.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can you share an example of a clever way a villain was defeated?
Answer: I can share several! First up, a bit of a cheat. It happens a lot, and it’s often in a very clever way. Because Venom is stronger, faster, more versatile and knows Peter, he really has to outsmart Venom to win. Ebony Maw was extremely powerful, and that’s with an inherently powerful ability: telekinesis. Weak telekinetics are very hard to deal with, Maw was next level. Luckly, Peter watched some movies. After Spider-Man gave the idea, Stark very quickly killed Ebony by blasting a hole open for the void of space to suck Maw out. This has to be one of the most iconic “smart ways a villain was defeated” A bit of stretch, but I like it.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If you didn't care for Star Wars Andor what would be the reasons?
Answer: I am looking forward to watching it some time. But the reception I have seen has made it clear that the main critique is the slowness. A lot of people find it boring; some find it excruciatingly boring. And contrary to the opinions of a couple fans, that is a valid critique. While I think the show will be amazing and find positive reviews to be more reasoned, the objective quality of a show can’t only be measured in what the show in question is good at. A good hook is important to any story, Andor hasn’t exactly been popular for its first episodes, even with fans. So, those are valid reasons to not care for Andor, although it seems like a great show to me, and I look forward to watching it.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why is Darth Vader so famous?
Answer: I mean… how could he not be? Darth Vader was the main antagonist in one of the most popular movies of all time, not just Si-Fi. And he just hit really well as a villain. He was terrifying, he was powerful, cold, he had his own theme music to compliment his enterence! That opening scene is honestly one of the most iconic enterences ever. Vader was an untsopable beast that made one question, “can he be beat?” And his design is generally accepted as very cool. Darth Vader is as popular as he is because he was part of a huge franchisee - Star Wars - and is everything you could ask for in a villain. He simply made you feel things when he came on screen. And that unmistakeable presence is what made him an icon.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Where was Ashoka during Order 66? If she was not on Coruscant like Anakin, where was she and what was she doing at the time?
Answer: She was flying away from the siege of Mandalore. But to be frank, she was in one really bad position. The ship had few places to run and was absolutely packed with clones. Ahsoka was in one of the worst situations of any Jedi during Order 66. But thanks to Anakin’s training, Tano would survive. Some credit should also go to Maul and Ahsoka’s own wit.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is the most powerful video game character in your opinion?
Answer: I haven't played every game, so I don't know the objective answer, but I'll answer based on games I've played. Then, it's between ATLAS He is the computer running the simulation of the No Man's Sky reality (the lore is insane there) And the other would be STEVE He can lift trillions of pounds on a bad day; the scaling is nuts.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the difference between a Jedi and a Jedi master?
Answer: “Jedi” is broad, “Jedi Master” is specific. One is part of the other. For example, Obi-Wan throughout all these stages: Was a Jedi. But he was only a Jedi Master between AotC and RotS The Jedi ranks are include These are young children whom their parents sent to become Jedi. They are often referred to as “younglings”. After an initiate has finished basic training, the Jedi will be assigned to a Knight or Master to be trained 1 on 1 and go on missions. After facing trials, Padawans become Knights, an accomplished Jedi that can protect the endangered from most threats they might face. Truly exceptional Knights are given the rank of Master for outstanding performances and acts of heroism. Not just that, but also great display of knowledge, understanding and resolve. When someone talks about a “Jedi”, that person will most likely be talking about some character who is at least a Padawan, while in-universe most people talk about Knights only. But the average person on Star Wars was not so educated on the Jedi.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the Sith Code in Star Wars Legends and what does it represent?
Answer: The Sith Code is based off of the Jedi Code, and it represents the philosophy of the Sith and what they live by. Peace is a lie, there is only passion Through passion, I gain strength Through strength, I gain power Through power, I gain victory Through victory, my chains will be broken The Force shall free me Lots of “I gain”, selfishness and hunger. Also, a beautiful summing up of the Sith life in general. They think the Dark Side will free them, when it is actually the only trap they’re in. And a fun fact: Sam Writer put the Sith Code in the Canon (sort of) Famous voice actor of Maul and massive Star Wars nerd (also actor for The Grand Inquisitor+Starkiller) While Darth Maul was crazy and needed to mumble things, Sam decided to make those mumbles parts of the Sith Code because he wanted it to officially be Canon. Whether or not he succeeded is up to you.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who wins, Plo Koon or Anakin Skywalker?
Answer: Anakin. As amazing as Plo Koon is, he is not enough to match a prime Skywalker. With some specific versions, Plo could definitely win, but overall, I must say Skywalker is the more powerful of the two. And more skilled. Plo Koon barely has any feats in the Canon, while Anakin probably has more screentime than anyone. Not just that, but it’s filled with very impressive feats. He was a constant match for Kenobi (who could fight Savage + Maul in a tunnel) While Plo Koon lost to Savage alone (through less direct methods, but the point stands) Anakin Skywalker is a legendary Jedi, one that accomplished almost every impossible task he was given. He matched Ventress, Dooku, and much much more.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are some tips for writing good answers on Quora?
Answer: There are so many great tips in the answer, so I do recommend checking some of those out later. But there is a lot missing. The big tips are covered, but for one problem, there are smaller things left out. You’re writing changes naturally throughout your Quoran journey, but it actually also needs to. Sometimes you hit a speed bump, sometimes you hit a stop. You will need to adjust sometimes. I know it sounds stupid; it is if you always do it. But even if it’s once a year, I think it’s a good idea to challenge yourself to write a long answer. Can you write something so engaging and helpful that it keeps attention for long? Because what’s not said often is that great long-answers are often what make people follow, and it’s a good test of a writer. Even good answers can be boring. Honestly, there is so much of the same stuff everywhere. Good grammar, phrasing, images, paragraphing; all of that can be done and leave a reader unsatisfied. Do not let your answer blend in if you can avoid it. One defining quality of a Quran legend - to me - is some unique quirk. Even if I can't place my finger on why I can, I want to be able to tell who wrote what answer without seeing a profile. Let evidence say that. Be right, don't say you are such. Reading someone be so sure of themselves makes people wish there was a “subtract a follow” button and want to disagree. Be humble and on the same level as the reader. And then the big thing that’s left out: There’s no one way to write. Quora writing is not making a novel, it is a unique form of writing, contained in a fascinating social media platform. Sure, the algorithm might favor a way, but a well-known tip is to be passionate and write what you feel like writing. You must be comfortable with going off script sometimes. Consider advice, but know when you can’t apply it and stay true to your form of writing. Not everyone loves to write medium-length answers on fiction, not everyone loves to write two-liners. If you aim to dominate a field (like the MCU) look at top MCU writers and answers. (Example: more scaling -like answers on how powerful people are do quite well) If you want to dominate Star Wars, look at top Star Wars writers and answers. (Example: there, comparing Star Wars to other parts of itself is popular) There are undeniably many parts of Quora. You will find readers who don’t like fiction, some who want politics, and some who love DC. Know which part you want to be in and apply relevant tips. Not only that, self-teach yourself some. That answer is brilliant, by the way, I recommend reading that too. For people who know what they’re doing - like Crantzer, The God Butcher and Nathan Stanish - how was this?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do Jedi and Sith use energy shields? If not, why not?
Answer: Energy shields? Not really. Almost all Jedi use Force Shields; and since the Force has been described as an energy field, you could say yes. Although I think it’s misleading. Force Shields are mostly to protect from Force attacks but can also be manifested as a bubble. When I think of an energy shield in Star Wars, I think of a Mandalorian combat shield, personal shields (like on Destroyers) Or these huge things: And they don’t use such shields because they don’t need to. Jedi can sense attacks and move at incredible speeds. With a lightsaber, they have a meta-shield. Remember Ahsoka during Order 66? That and some of the best dodging skills in the galaxy. Jedi are such good shields, in fact, they cover up for more than themselves! They are often in front lines, before any clones, deflecting bolts that might come for their fellow soldiers.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In a hypothetical battle, who would win between Thanos with the Infinity Stones and Grand Admiral Thrawn from Star Wars?
Answer: Thanos wins with no Infinity Stones! This is a grand mismatch. One of the most powerful beings in the MARVEL universe up against a strategist. Sure, Thrawn’s impressive; even in physical aspects, he’s fit and trained. But he’s a match for humans, not a Titan! Throw in the Infinity Stones and you have a super obvious winner who will actually win with no difficulty whatsoever. The only thing Thrawn has going for him is intelligence. Knowledge is power and all, but it’s not infinity-stone kind of power.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is the Thrawn trilogy considered part of the official Canon in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: Unfortunately, it is not. It was removed to make room for the sequel trilogy, like a massive chunk of Legends. In my opinion, one of the worst parts about Disney’s separation of Canon and Legends is that they removed some things for no apparent reason. Why on earth remove comics that take place just before TPM when it conflicts with nothing?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If you could be best friends with any fictional character, who would you choose?
Answer: This guy: Tom’s Peter Parker, from the MCU. I just find him so relatable. Most people do (talking about Spider-Man overall) He is made to be relatable. And this version specifically really sticks with me. He is fun, friendly, does well with school (specifically science) and is just someone I’d love to be friends with personality wise.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why does Peter Parker not want to be Iron Man?
Answer: It’s not all fun and games being Iron Man. Peter is still a kid. He’s been through a lot, a lot a lot, but still. Iron Man was an adult and one of the greatest superheroes ever. He fought off the Chitari in New York, he helped save the world against his own creation (after it chose to skew its creator’s vision; Tony made a mistake, but it’s not all his fault) Tony Stark also ended up giving his life to save the universe from Thanos. Not just that, but he was also incredibly good at keeping his reputation squeaky clean. Well, as clean as possible; the people loved him. Now, is a broke teenager like Peter Parker really ready for all that? No. Spidey just is not ready and may very well never be. Tony was special (as Peter is special, in a different way) If Peter does make “Iron Man” a mantle, and it’s done well, I’ll be all for it. But as of now, Peter’s just not ready. He knows it, and he knows being Iron Man isn't all money and parties.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who was Tony Stark's best friend in the MCU?
Answer: I must go with Rhodey over Happy. While both were close, there’s an important thing missing between Happy and Tony: They are not equals, or to put it more clearly, Happy won’t give a slap to Tony when he needs one. Rhodes, on the other hand, would. He truly cares for Tony and will do what’s best for him. These are real brothers. Tony wouldn’t sacrifice for Happy on the same level he would for Rhodes. And their relationship has proved strong through much tribulation. Yes, this is Tony Stank

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are your thoughts on Earth-17628?
Answer: Main thought: very underrated. No, extremely underrated! It’s one of those new shows with a more basic art style than the previous show, which was more basic than the first, and these shows are often bad, but Earth-17628 is different. The first season of MARVEL’S SPIDER-MAN going nowhere justifies much criticism, but it gets progressively better, seriously, way better. And you know what? This series takes gambles few do these days. Quite a few of my favorite versions of characters come from this verse. Earth-17628 has given many awesome designs, character adaptations, and plots better than many originals. And even if they’re not all better, the fresh take is just so… refreshing! Examples: Personally, I found this version decent. New enough, nice great design. My joint-favorite MARVEL character. They did him justice. Even though he was not a focus, the bits we see are amazing, and they show how formidable and smart Tony is. What I love about him most is the suit diversity. In the MCU, we see improvement, but no specialization outside of the Hulkbuster. The designs are so awesome, and the functions are unique and exciting. My favorite Harry to date. He’s not like the originally, but I honestly prefer this one. This Osborn feels like someone Parker would be friends with. Great match. And he’s just more interesting and cooler in my subjective view. So fresh! I loved his role in the closing arc. So much mystery sounds him, but he proved to be a hero. I wish it were more likely they would continue work on this verse. “Great shoes” is all I’ll say. And outside of those who came first to my mind, look at these other designs: Makes me wish they tried harder at the art.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can time travel be achieved like in the movie "Doctor Strange"?
Answer: … Magic? Time travel wasn’t even really in Doctor Strange, there was just the manipulation of time on certain objects and people. But either way, that type of time-”faffing” is not achievable here. Time travel overall though? It’s highly debatable. (Let me know your thoughts on it) Personally, I don’t think we can build any time machine. I don’t think anything physical can manipulate the dimension of time. We are very accepted as beings limited and bound by time. We can only make things bound by the three dimensions we’re comfortable with, hence I do not think time travel is possible. + the time paradox is something I think would stop us from changing anything through time travel.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What happened to Luke after the events of Return of the Jedi? Are there any books or other sources that discuss this topic?
Answer: After Return of the Jedi, Luke’s journey splits. In Legends, he founds a great new Jedi Order and becomes the most powerful Jedi of all. he fights and protects the galaxy from Sidious, “The Mother”, Vong and much more. In Canon, we have a bit less of Luke post-RotJ He appears with a new order in The Book of Boba Fett, and shows his CGI’d face in the Mandalorian. Other than that, all we have of post-RotJ Luke in Canon is from the sequels.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: I don't understand power scaling, what is the appeal?
Answer: LOL, same here for a while. I think the main appeal of normal scaling is about the following two things: That makes scaling a fun way to practice school. And it’s a flex for some people. So, that must seem useful and make it look like the best way to do anything related to assessing the power of a character (that is why it’s called “scaling”)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the age difference between Luke and Grogu (Baby Yoda)?
Answer: Grogu 50 during The Mandalorian’s first season. Which takes place during 9 ABY So, Baby Yoda is 41 by A New Hope, whereas Luke is only 19! That Makes Grogu 22 years older than Luke Skywalker. Very strange, very strange indeed.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
