Answer: Here’s my take on the main distinctions: Dark Jedi: Sith:

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Was Luke Skywalker the last of the old Jedi order?
Answer: I think Order 66 killed the old Jedi. Luke was taught by Jedi from the old Order, but Luke himself was more like the first Jedi of the new Order. He wasn’t taught like other Jedi were, the temple was gone, he was never a real Padawan, just sub-Knight. His whole experience was unique, and it definitely did not resemble the experiences of Jedi from the old Order.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Luke Skywalker die in Star Wars: The Last Jedi?
Answer: He drained himself past the point of exhaustion, and felt he had completed his story, done all he needed to do, and thus surrendered to the Cosmic Force and became a part of it. And I think it was handled very well, ignoring previous films. Luke’s sacrifice was of perfect importance: very needed, but not overly flashy. This way he didn’t outshine Rey, but still met a dignified and meaningful end.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't Anakin just come clean and tell Obi Wan about his inner turmoil? Wouldn't Obi Wan have help him since he cared about him?
Answer: This is a very sad and complex topic. Wouldn't Obi Wan have helped him since he cared about him? Absolutely. In fact, I’m sure Obi-Wan would have helped Anakin in whatever way was needed, even if it meant leaving the Order. Anakin was by far the most important person in Kenobi’s life. Anakin was made about not being a master for two reasons. One was because the rank granted further access to the library. Obi-Wan could have shared anything Anakin wanted. And if Anakin did come to Kenobi, there is absolutely a chance that he never would have fell. But: Why didn't Anakin just come clean and tell Obi Wan about his inner turmoil? Anakin has long been rolling downhill. It hard to confess, and he did not see Obi-Wan for what he was. Palpatine worked hard to make himself the father figure of Anakin, the go-to for wisdom. While Anakin thought Obi-Wan was jealous, and too strict. Sidious was the only person Anakin felt safe with (aside from Padme) And Obi-Wan had systematically lost influence over Anakin. With Kenobi, I genuinely think Anakin could overcome the extreme grooming of Palpatine. Anakin almost let Mace kill Palpatine and had many other moments of confliction. If Obi-Wan was accepted more by Anakin, it is very likely that the tragedy of Vader could have been avoided. I personally think George tried to convey the message with some scenes.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: We all know that Sidious is the Chancellor, but why did he become the Chancellor in the first place?
Answer: Well, aside from much shady business, Palpatine seemed to be the perfect candidate. He’s an elderly, apparently wise, royal from Naboo and previously successful senator. Palpatine hid his true colors very well. And played his cards even better. The timing and set up were perfect.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How incomplete was the training of Luke Skywalker in Star Wars? Why?
Answer: In A New Hope Luke’s training barely started. And it showed; all he did was sense basic things initiates could sense. By the time of ESB, after a week or so with Yoda and more training beforehand, Luke was a skilled Jedi. Not up there with the best, but thanks to his instincts, determination, and ridiculously high midi-chlorian count, he was definitely above most Jedi and capable of escaping Vader’s trap. Which is very impressive, even though Vader was being held back, it’s still Vader we’re talking about. So, his training was decent. And by Return of the Jedi, Luke is a very formidable Jedi. By that time, his training was complete (in terms of combat; all he had left was to finalize the strengthening of his character by confronting his father) And then we get a glimpse of GM Skywalker, which seems to be the peak of the character.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Anakin's arrogance contribute to his loss against Obi-Wan? Did he have any chance of winning the fight?
Answer: Contribute? It was the main cause of his defeat. Anakin had a huge chance of winning, that much is clear! Multiple times throughout the fight, Obi-Wan came very close to losing. At one point, Skywalker was the only one with a weapons and Kenobi was slowing the blade coming for his neck. And Obi-Wan had Anakin in almost the same situation. It was not just a close fight; it was the closest in Star Wars history. The fight was back and forth, 50/50 throughout, waiting for someone to gain an upper hand for real. And that deciding disadvantage ended up being a foolish tactic from Anakin.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can Luke, at the time of Return of the Jedi, beat an Inquisitor?
Answer: He could probably wreck an inquisitor by the time of ESB. Actually, not just probably. In a comic he defeated the Grand Inquisitor right after ESB (a good while before RotJ) You may be thinking, “but he was dead!”, in which case you would be a very knowledgeable fan and right; but after the Grand Inquisitor said there are things worse than death, he sadly got to feel it first-hand. Vader bound his spirit, and that’s how he could fight Luke.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Luke know where to find Yoda on Dagobah?
Answer: In regard to the specific location on the planet? We don’t know. The fans only hear Obi-Wan’s Force Ghost tell Luke to go to Dagobah for training. Maybe Luke just sensed the perfect spot, maybe it was fate, we may never know for sure.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Does Luke ever learn about Ahsoka Tano being Anakin Skywalker’s Padawan?
Answer: From Ahsoka herself! In the Book of Boba Fett, she even mentions how similar Luke and Anakin are. (Questionable, I know) While it is not totally confirmed, it is far more than likely that Luke knows Tano was Anakin’s Padawan. As for when they met or when it might have happened, we are still in the dark. I, for one, am very excited to see more of GM Luke Skywalker in the Canon. That era is honestly a really good one in-universe; and one I find very interesting.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Luke Skywalker utilize Vaapad to defeat Darth Vader in Return of the Jedi?
Answer: No, Luke did not even know what Vaapad was. Dang, he didn’t even know Force Lightning existed! And really, Luke “utilized” nothing to beat Vader. Saying ‘Vader lost’ is more accurate than saying ‘Luke won’ in my opinion. By RotJ Luke Skywalker was an absolute legend of a Jedi, very powerful. But Vader is in another league; Luke could only walk out alive because papa Darth was conflicted (so conflicted that his character arc was about close with a U turn)

Question: What do jedi do with a defeated enemy when there is no organization behind them to take the foe prisoner? If a jedi himself is in hiding, and the enemy is too dangerous to set free.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What kind of emperor would Anakin have been if he'd won against Obi-Wan on Mustafar and gone on to overthrow Palpatine?
Answer: A really terrible tyrant whom someone else (most likely with an understanding of politics) would eventually overthrow. It would not happen quickly; Vader is far too powerful and intimidating. But millions of subjects wanting you gone? While it is not exactly irrecoverable, the only way you’re staying on top is by knowing how to manipulate hoards like that. Anakin just lacked the political ability necessary to be the tyrant he envisioned himself to be. Well, to stay the tyrant for long. There’s even a chance of removal by force. In the hypothetical, there’s a room for anything to happen; Yoda could fight Vader, Luke, Ezra, etc. Not to mention that where would probably be more people inspired to become rebels. I see this “Empower Vader” having even more enemies than Palpatine, to be honest.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Star-Lord choose to hit Thanos instead of taking the glove from him with his free hand in Infinity War?
Answer: He was angry. Like how Thor was angry. The difference is one of them can actually match Thanos. Star-Lord was totally blinded by anger, and it is completely reasonable. Thanos took Gamora from Quill; I don’t really blame him one bit.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What happened to General Grievous after Revenge of the Sith? Where is he during A New Hope? How come we never see him again in any other movie after that one?
Answer: Well, It would make sense that we don’t see him after this: Kenobi got him with multiple blaster bolts straight to vital organs (the last he had left) General Grievous was as dead as dead could be.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is General Grievous pure evil?
Answer: No, he’s broken. In Canon, there was an orchestrated accident (I’d say that’s not enough for him to be broken, but it does make “pure evil” a slight stretch in my opinion; we have Palpatine in SW, the standards are low, very, very low) And in the EU this guy is undeniably, utterly broken. (After that, he becomes almost as evil as evil can be, but I assume “pure evil” in this context means evil for no reason from the get-go)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is better, Commander Gree or Commander Wolfe?
Answer: I must say Commander Wolffe. Gree was great in the Bad Batch for a bit, but so did Wolffe. They both resisted the Empire for friends. While neither provided resistance to Order 66 at the time it was sent out, Wolffe didn’t have a chance to. I think he absolutely would not have shot down Plo Koon if he was given the chance. Wolffe and Plo Koon were arguably closer together than Ahsoka and Rex! Plus, I just find Wolffe more interesting in terms of history, character and relationships. He has more screentime too. I really think a lot of General Koon rubbed off on Wolffe. He’s also one of the 3 we saw in Rebels. One well-fed wolf

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why do people say that Kylo is weaker than Vader if he had killed off an entire Jedi Temple and caught a blaster bolt in midair something Vader couldn't do?
Answer: Because Kylo’s power isn’t shown well, and a lot of people hate anything related to the sequels. And Kylo Ren froze a bolt by using Force Stasis (an ability Vader did not use) Simply knowing the ability does not put Kylo above Vader, the latter could react just as fast. And Vader is Canonically the most powerful Sith of all time in the Disney Canon. I know Kylo is not a Sith, but do you really think Kylo is more impressive than Palpatine? But feats are greater than statements. Ren has his fair share of feats, but as cool as Kylo is, I honestly think he’s outclassed with this one.

A well-matured, simply good soul that’s the best of the best. (Seriously, he’s the Magnus Carlson of Star Wars and champion of MARVEL right now) I hope to reach that height in the SW community. No. 1 in topics unnumbered. Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't TIE Fighters have a hyperdrive and shields to begin with?
Answer: Because TIE fighters were not meant to be good. This is what happens when politicians are in control of things they have no business with. Tarkin thought “numbers” was the answer. “Let’s have 1,000 blunt arro- no - let’s have 10,000 bubbles!” TIEs were not quite that bad, but they were horrible and some of the worst fighters ever made in Star Wars. Bad view, no shields, no hyperdrive and more. The Empire already had ridiculous numbers, the idea behind TIEs was stupid. That thing didn’t even have life-support, the suits had to have those functions. In fairness, the Empire had to do dumb things like this for the Rebels to win; the writers were forced.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If Peter Parker was gone for 5 years due to the “blip” in Infinity War/End Game, why weren’t his classmates older in Spider-man: Far From Home?

Question: Why can Thanos pick up Thor's axe?
Answer: Because Stormbreaker has no enchantment about worthiness. Stormbreaker is just an incredibly powerful weapon with the power to summon the Bifrost and better channel/amplify Thor’s power. Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is your unpopular opinion about the main characters in The Clone Wars series, aside from Anakin and Ahsoka?
Answer: I have a few for each! Ahsoka Tano: Anakin Skywalker: Obi-Wan Kenobi:

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which is more powerful, the dark saber or the lightsaber?
Answer: I guess the Darksaber. Normal lightsabers and the unique Darksaber seem to have equal cutting ability, so there I think they are tied. But what makes the Darksaber special is its responsiveness. To someone untrained, it fights, it becomes heavy, but to people who know how to wield it, the Darksaber evidently becomes an amplifier. And there is another advantage: the Darksaber pulls lightsabers, this will be natural for the one holding the Darksaber, but throw off the opponent.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Obi-Wan Kenobi's power and skill underrated?
Answer: Overall, Obi-Wan is not underrated. He’s too popular for that. But skill-wise, people often forget just how astounding he is. Kenobi could fight Maul and Savage, in a 2v1, and in a cave! And not only that, but he survived and walked away relatively fine (Savage lost an arm) Obi-Wan also consistently proves himself comparable to Anakin (and most of us know how powerful he is) While, in terms of dueling and Force power, Anakin may be superior to Obi-Wan, it is never enough to beat him quickly, and it’s never enough to cover up for one mistake he always ends up making. Simply surviving Anakin’s offense is the main feat I am pointing at here. Obi-Wan Kenobi has beaten Ventress (TCW movie), General Grievous (RotS) and he also forced Jango Fett to retreat. His skill is also very incredible. Kenobi has mastered his form (Soresu) so well that he is undisputably its best practitioner; few can penetrate his defense. Obi-Wan only seems weak sometimes because he’s very humble and even more brave. The people he faces are people few others are willing to fight.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How successful would the rebels be in a battle against Thrawn?
Answer: In a battle? That is beyond vague. How many Rebels? How many Imperials? Where? What is each side’s goal? We need to know at least a bit more to decide reasonably. If it’s anywhere near even, I see Thrawn’s team winning. But never say never: The Rebels often have aces up their sleeves.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What characters would you like to see in Tales of the Jedi Season 2? Personally I’d love to see Baylan Skoll or Plo Koon get their own arcs
Answer: Honestly, same here. Baylan and Shin are begging for backstory and Plo Koon simply needs more material. Greatly set up canvases and a hidden gem, what combination could be better to explore? Otherwise, I would like to finally see Luke Skywalker handled by people who made TCW and other prequels era projects so we can finally compare properly.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did the separatists ever really have a chance of winning against the Republic in Star Wars?
Answer: Despite what people think, no. Not naturally. People forget how much was done just to set up a half decent position for the CIS. Palpatine had to throw hyperspace lanes and a good economy (not just away from the Republic, but to the Confederacy) If Palpatine didn’t pull strings with the banking clans and mess with the money in other ways, the droid army would not have been possible. And he also purposefully ran the Republic economy into the ground (mid-war) which led to fewer clones than there would have been naturally. But it is all about speculation with what if questions.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are the primary forms of light saber combat utilized by the Jedi Order?
Answer: Cool There are seven classical form of lightsaber combat. # Form I: Shii-Cho This is the most basic form. It is taught to all Padawans and contains simple, long strokes (predictable to more experienced duelists) Most notable user: Kit Fisto # Form II: Makashi Makashi was made when Sith and Jedi both had lightsabers. It is for intricate, efficient and elegant dueling (mostly done with one hand) Most notable user: Count Dooku # Form III: Soresu This was made for deflecting and redirecting blaster fire, but it doubles as a very defensive combat style. Most notable user: Obi-Wan Kenobi # Form IV: Ataru This form is the most draining, and most dangerous. It’s all about movement, jumps, flips, rolls etc. Most notable user: Yoda # Form V: Djem So/Shien This is the style of two halves. One is about strong, powerful blows: good offense. And the other is defense and counterattacks (mostly about blaster bolts to be extremely well rounded) Most notable user: Anakin Skywalker # Form VI: Niman Niman is also known as the diplomat’s form. It is a jack of all trades, master of none. But it has focus on one thing: the Force As you can tell, it’s questionable in terms of lightsaber-to-lightsaber combat. Most notable user: Qui-Gon (debatable) # Form VII: Juyo This is super aggressive and tied to feelings/instincts. It is powerful, random, and hard to deal with. But also dangerous to use; the Jedi did not teach it regularly. Most notable user: Mace Windu (with his own variant: Vaapad) or Maul for plain Juyo

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is it possible for Anakin to defeat Yoda in a lightsaber duel? If not, who would win in a match between the two?
Answer: Ok, easy part first: If [it is not possible for Anakin to defeat Yoda], who would win in a match between the two? In the case that it’s impossible for Anakin to win, I must say I’d place my bet on Yoda. Now for the harder one: Is it possible for Anakin to defeat Yoda in a lightsaber duel? Yes. In Legends, Plo Koon beat Yoda in a duel, and as much as I hate to say it, Anakin is definitely Plo’s superior. And they use the same form. While Anakin is very unlikely to win, it is absolutely possible. So, I still think I’ll place my bet on Yoda.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How do I begin with the Star Wars franchise? I’ve never seen a movie of it or any books about it. I have no knowledge of Star Wars. What are some tips for being a beginner?
Answer: In chronological order, like a professional. For tips, I would recommend not watching everything in order, just the main bits. And definitely to keep the following in mind: Star Wars is many things. The main thing I mean by this is that you will dislike some Star Wars projects and love others. We have the originally trilogy, which is an old, classic masterpiece and one of the greatest examples of the hero’s journey. And then we have the prequels which was made to be expansive and somewhat experimental for George’s own way of storytelling (and since George wasn’t good with dialogue, it’s definitely not flawless) but nonetheless, it’s more complex and action packed, so it’s my favorite. Then we have the Mandalorian, a more western masterpiece. And Andor, a show with powerful dialogue, but less action. And the clone wars, a balance between the originals and prequels in the form of a series. So, don’t expect shows and movies to be similar. Now, if you’re wondering about the order, here it is. The legend of my “map”: Now, what did I miss?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How important are strong female characters in the Star Wars saga?
Answer: Very. From an out-of-universe view, you just have to have them. Why limit such a huge universe to a smaller audience? But from an in-universe point of view, it gets wild. So, an obvious one is Rey, she is arguably the most important character ever. (It is not my opinion that she is, but it’s arguable) Then we have Hera, Jyn, and a few more women who played huge roles in the rebellion. We also have Padme, whose role in Star Wars is beyond massive. She was the mother of Luke and maybe the biggest part of Anakin’s life/fall (other than Palpatine) But my main pick is Leia Organa! Imagine the OG team without her; it's not pretty. I think her role in Luke’s life (the main hero overall in my opinion) and her role in the rebellion are absolutely vital to how things played out. The Rebellion and OG team relied a lot on Leia; she is undeniably one of the most important characters in Star Wars.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In Star Wars, how do you use “the force”? Does it use your life force or stamina or can you use it infinitely? Do you recharge it by sleeping or eating or even meditating and such?
Answer: Using the Force requires different things depending on what the desired ability is. It ranges from focus to unhinged emotion. And I think - as unprofessional as it sounds - it is safe to think of it as a video-game style bar. Something like a “Force tank” does exist. The Force can be exercised like a muscle, and it drains its own kind of stamina. And you can recharge by laying off using it for a while or meditating!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Luke Skywalker have to go through training if he was already powerful? Could Yoda have trained him from the beginning?
Answer: He was not already powerful, he had potential. Natural affinity, but no knowledge of how to use his gift, nor any experience using it. His high potential from Anakin made the training faster and easier, but without training, Luke would not have gone far.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do you agree that Anakin Skywalker seemed to turn to the dark side a tad too quickly in Revenge of the Sith?
Answer: If it was just about becoming evil, Anakin definitely turned way too abruptly. We all know Palpatine was manipulating Anakin and setting him up for years. (Most of his life by RotS) So, Anakin’s fall makes sense, but the speed? That seems a little out of proportions. But it happened so incredibly because of how the Dark Side works. Anakin wasn’t just turning on his ethics, he gave in to the Dark Side. And The Dark Side consumed most of Anakin in the instant he decided to fall to it; that changed his mind, his perspective, his nature. Anakin turned so massively because that’s how the Dark Side works in Star Wars. It consumes like a fire, twists so quickly because the Dark Side is a trap. Not something you can just tap into. Once the Dark Side lured you it, it snaps shut, and doesn't let go.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What happened to Ahsoka after she escaped Order 66? Did she ever reunite with Captain Rex again?
Answer: After Order 66, Ahsoka became “Ashla” and went into hiding. Ahsla was almost the name of the Light Side, and then also almost Ahsoka’s original name She becomes as simple as she can be, she tries to stay lowkey, but it doesn’t work out so well. After this period of her life (which lasts quite long) She becomes Fulcrum! One of many informants for the Rebellion. It is during this period of time that she reunites with Captain Rex. And if you haven’t seen the scene, it’s definitely one you should watch. What a heart warmer. Ahsoka goes through even more phases of life (like the one we see in her series) When destiny calls, heroes never ignore it for long. And Ahsoka Tano just happens to be one of those heroes.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which Star Wars TV show do you think has done the best job at expanding the lore of the franchise?
Answer: Expanding? Interesting question! And the answer simply must be The Clone Wars. Come on, seven full seasons worth of content, filling up the big gap between AotC and RotS; how could that be topped! The Clone Wars added tons of lore and characters. It added planets, schemes, extra story for existing characters (Dooku, but mostly Maul!) And it did not stop at normal side characters, it made some massive ones. Like Ahsoka, one of the most beloved Star Wars characters ever. And we also have Ventress, Rex (it’s also responsible for almost all of Plo Koon’s screentime) But another huge thing it added was classic story telling and action to the prequel era. (We all know George was feeling spicey when he made those; TCW really helped the prequels be more well-received, and it did great things for Star Wars in the sense)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the rating for Star Wars and why is it not higher than PG?
Answer: Because most of the time, Star Wars is not just for the men, but the women, and the children too.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why are sequels never as good as the original films?
Answer: Even though sequels can be better, original films are very often better than follow ups, and here’s why: The example film Now, think about some sequels that were better than the earlier films. In my opinion, Captain America: The Winter Soldier, Spider-Man: No Way Home, and a few other MCU movies would come to mind. You know what sets them apart? Planning! When a movie is made with a clear future in the minds of developers, they set up those movies to come. But this is very rarely the case. Most films do not have planned sequels, and the lack of planning for a next story is the root of the main problem: the characters arcs Great stories are almost all character driven. You have a hero, he has an arc. And that arc will define the character. Take Miles, for example. His arc finished, the defining period of his story was covered in Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse. Miles became Spider-Man, the other characters came with internal conflict, and left victorious. Now, why could Across the Spider-Verse not hit as hard as the first film? There can only be one main arc. Miles’ story ended (for the most part) His main arc was defined, you cannot just make a new one; that would rewrite the character you’ve defined. The next arc must be smaller, and in a character driven story, that means the film overall will have less internal conflict/impact. I think this is why sequels rarely outdo originals. The Spider-Verse team hit it out of the park with the first and second. But with this answer in mind, I expected exactly what I got with ATSV It had to have more plot, less drive. And because of the amazing team, it was near as good as it could be.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is the Dark Side truly part of the Force, or just a perversion of it?
Answer: In most new parts of the Canon, the Dark Side is a natural part of the Force. Disney made the duality of the Force like a Ying and Yang. But in lots of the Disney Canon and almost all of the old Canon, the Dark Side is a perversion of the Light Side. An unnatural creation of corrupt Force-Users corrupting the Force inside themselves. Sith Code vs the Jedi Code, simply to add some information to this Quora short.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In your opinion, was Luke's character ruined in Star Wars: The Force Awakens?
Answer: I would say the Sequels did nothing too unreasonable with Luke on surface level. Is it wrong for a character to change after many, many years and huge, life-changing disasters? No, that is absolutely fine. But Disney did break my favorite part of Luke: he cannot be broken. In Return of the Jedi, I left thinking Luke faced his trials, he withstood pressure and came out stronger. In my head, he went on to be the perfect Jedi (or close) Like a teen matured into an adult, ready to face anything life throws at him. But apparently, he gave up after something I think a lesser Luke would not have given in to. And - as the great redeeming of Star Wars, the guy who saw good in Vader - the way he handled his vision of Ben was pretty much the nail in the coffin for the version of Luke Skywalker I loved.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win: Plo Koon or Ki-Adi-Mundi?
Answer: Plo Koon. In Canon, Ki-Adi Mundi has the epic feat of existing. While Plo Koon (while he has very few feats) at least has a couple of good achievements. Like his encounter with Aurra Sing. And in Legends, Plo thrives. Let Master Jared show you!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win: Rex or Cody?
Answer: Captain Rex, most likely. Sure, Cody has a higher rank, but that’s only because Ahsoka took the place of commander for the 501st. Also, Cody was more long-range based. In one-vs-one scenarios, I don’t think that will help very much. Rex also has way more to show. Feats-wise, Cody has very little.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which of the lightsaber forms of combat counter each other?
Answer: There are not many advantages and disadvantages between forms. Each was developed for a need existing forms did not fulfil, and they were all made by Jedi (who did not plan on fighting each other) So, they are not intentional or large in number, but here: Djem So > Makashi (Vaapad also works great against it, maybe even more so) Makashi was made for dueling, but it was made before Djem So. The intricacy of Form II gets completely disturbed and disrupted by the massive strikes of Djem So, which force “surviving”. Soresu > Djem So (Ataru works much worse than Form V against Soresu, but I’m getting to a circle) Soresu is a pretty basic form at surface level. Honestly, I do see a conserving defense beating a draining offense when the styles are used by equally skilled fighters. The passive Soresu is the environment the artful Makashi thrives in. I think the definitive example of this form-vs-form matchup is in AotC where Dooku could expertly pick through Obi-Wan’s defense. So, the rock-paper-scissors of forms in my eyes is the above! Makashi > Soresu > Djem so > Makashi

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why is Samuel L. Jackson's lightsaber purple?
Answer: The reason is pretty funny, actually. It’s so he could spot himself easily in the Battle of Geonosis. At first, George did not want to change the Canon and add another colour, but he posted about it and that blew up, so, you could actually thank the fans for purple lightsabers. SLJ started it, but we ended it.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the worst thing George Lucas did to Star Wars?
Answer: Sell it. “Movie making is not a business, it’s an art form” He’s not the only person who could have it, and if he chose a successor, that successor may very well have continued to make even better things than George. George failed at important aspects of the moviemaking proses, but he invented Star Wars and largely pioneered CGI in movies. He loved his creation; and with his endless, amazing ideas, he just would not have done the kind of damage Disney has. Giving in was a mistake, even if he really wanted out. Lucas made and would have made mistakes, but I honestly think Star Wars would have been off far better sticking with its maker. Disney brought great things too, but overall, I’d say it did more damage (and Dave Filoni is laregly responsible for that good bit Disney has done)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What weaknesses did the TIE Defender have, and how did the Rebels exploit them?
Answer: There weren’t enough yet. I know what you’re looking for, but honestly, whatever weakness it had, it was small and going to be ironed out. The TIE Defenders were absolute masterpieces. And it’s obvious they would be! They were made by the Empire’s greatest military genius! The Empire’s choice to not listen to Thrawn (the one who knows the art of war best) for its military affairs was one of the main choices that lead to its demise. Thrawn knew project stardust was just a flashy way to lose trillions.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Would Ashoka have turned to the dark side if she had been trained by Yoda instead of Anakin?
Answer: Ahsoka would probably be more firmly stuck to the Light if anything. But it would cost her. While Yoda’s training may have been better than Anakin’s in many ways, Yoda would pass down the ultimate weakness of the Jedi: a narrow view. She would not develop her own view of the galaxy like she did in the Clone Wars. Her arc was largely based around her overcoming her own biases and learning to look from more angles (“Heroes on both sides” and “The Wrong Jedi” greatly show this part of her arc) If she was blind to the Jedi’s stubbornness, she would have not been half the character she is. And Yoda’s training would not prepare her for Order 66 like Anakin’s did.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Did Palpatine truly care for Anakin, despite saying otherwise to Vader in Revenge of the Sith?
Answer: Not at all. Palpatine is very unfeeling. He actually hated Vader (that’s how he could use Force Lightning on him) This absolutely crooked villain loved no one (except for himself, maybe)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are your favorite and least favorite species in Star Wars?
Answer: Top 3: Kel’Dor Butchered the anatomy, but still a nice picture. Kel’Dors have good culture, look amazing, and my favorite Star Wars character is Kel’Dor. (Can you guess who?) The Yoda Species The name is unknown and so is the species home world (even their origin) But all members of the species have been abnormally powerful in the Force and inclined to the Light Side. Togruta There are so many cool species that could take third place, but I decided on Togruta because they have a strong sense of togetherness and overcome obstacles. Now, bottom 3: Dug Despicable. They look nasty and are nasty. Neimoidian Only the greedy survive. The people of this species only look after number one. A bunch of cowards and scoundrels. Hutt These guys were probably literally made to be hated. They look exactly what they’re like. Just purely selfish and completely lacking of any self-control.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are your hot takes on 1v1 matchups (SW and Marvel)?
Answer: MARVEL: 1 Strange (Infinity War) beats Thor (Infinity War) 2 Iron Man beats Spider-Man (in general for both) 3 Spider-Man beats Cap (MCU for both) Star Wars: 1 Obi-Wan beats Anakin (Both TCW) 2 Plo Koon beats Fisto (Both Legends) 3 Yoda beats Palpatine (RotS rematch)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How does Palpatine's raw power compare to Thanos's without using Force abilities like lightning or telekinesis?
Answer: Palpatine’s raw power if the Force. Without it, he’s just an old man. Thanos could flick Sheev and he would be done. But with Force power, Palpatine no diffs too. He’s way above Wanda (Endgame) and she could definitely 1v1 Thanos.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What do you think are the best comic book series of the Star Wars franchise (both in Canon and Legends continuities)?
Answer: While I’ve almost consumed all of the Canon, I am new to Legends. I have not read a lot of comics, which is the main bit of Canon material I’m missing. But I’ve read a few, and the best so far is the Canon comic run, Yoda. I really did enjoy this. It took place little before the Empire Strikes Back, but had lots of flash backs to the Clone Wars and before. Great adventures, action and wisdom. The themes were great, the art was absolute fire (nothing tops that style for me) And it was simply a lot of fun to read.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the theme in the Star Wars movie?
Answer: For each of the first 6: 1 The Phantom Menace So, as for a theme, I would say there was not much of the theme. George didn’t want another OT, he wanted to make new types of movies. Hence the prequels were additions, not standalone. But aside from the most important part of the film that is - in my opinion - Anakin’s father figure/the road he will go down, I would say the movie has a focus on destiny. Can it be stopped? Does anything need to happen for it to come true? 2 Attack of the Clones This was where all the pieces fell into place for checkmate. Whereas TPM was the set up. If I had to pick a theme, I would go with “small seeds, massive trees”. Tiny little manipulations and events violently shaking the galaxy’s fate. Small things in Anakin’s life shape him while large moves are made also. (This was way more focused on the Star Wars universe than sending messages to ours) 3 Revenge of the Sith Dread it, run from it… The theme was about a hero’s fall. No one is truly immune to temptation and that, sadly, emotions can lead you to a dark path if you let them control you. 4 A New Hope This was classical storytelling! It followed one of the best executions of the hero's journey. The theme also revolved a little bit around destiny, but mostly never judge a book by its cover. Any farm boy could become a galaxy’s hero. 5 The Empire Strikes Back Facing your fear. That’s my takeaway (in hindsight) Even though Luke lost the fight with Vader, I’d say Luke walked away with a victory as well. “A coward dies a thousand times before his death, but the valiant taste of death but once. It seems to me most strange that men should fear, seeing that death, a necessary end, will come when it will come.” - Shakespear’s Julius Caesar 6 Return of the Jedi This one had the strongest theme in my eyes: redemption. It doesn’t matter what your past was if you’re willing to put it behind you, where it belongs. Someone will always see the good in you and it will always be there. And it will always be ready to take over.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do you think Anakin could have taken the Jedi master's in duels?
Answer: Oh, absolutely. I mean… 99 percent of the time…. There was only one Jedi that could evenly match him (Obi-Wan) and only 2 that could and would beat him (Yoda and Mace Windu) And even that is highly debated. But Anakin Skywalker would pretty much school most Council members. And if we count every Jedi Master, he’d reck almost everyone. Kit Fisto, Shaak Ti, Adi-Gallia, Ki-Adi, etc. All of those Jedi do not stand much of a chance.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Palpatine more powerful than Darth Plagueis?
Answer: Depends on the time. By the time Palpatine overthrew Plagueis? Absolutely not. Sheev was very scared of his master and was probably even terrified as he came to attack his master while he slept. But a few years after? Palpatine definitely surpassed his master. The Emperor was the most powerful Sith of all time in the old Canon, and he’s not far off in the Disney Canon. I highly doubt Palpatine - in his prime - is less powerful than Plagueis in any Canon. It is the nature of the Rule of Two for the apprentice to slice and surpass the master.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the meaning of "BBY" in the context of measuring time in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: Before the Battle of Yavin There is also an ABY (A for “After”) As far as we’ve seen, this is not an in-universe way of measuring time. The people in Star Wars don’t use the BBY/ABY system, but it’s helpful for us (and even more the Goerge and other creators since it’s based around the time on the first movie)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is the main protagonist of the Star Wars saga?
Answer: The entire thing? I would say it’s split. Because Anakin’s story is a tragedy and by no means a classical hero’s tale, but still the most important, I give him the “main” and Luke the “protagonist” Turning good at the end doesn’t quite make Vader a protagonist; lots of movies end with the main antagonist turning good. Luke Skywalker was a classic and amazing protagonist/hero, while Anakin fell and became the main antagonist. But ultimately, Anakin’s choice to redeem himself was the pivot of the galaxy’s fate. The most important moment in Star Wars, and being honest, we all know Anakin’s life is the focus of Star Wars. Rey was the ending protagonist, not the main in my eyes. But Luke was the hero for the time around the turn. And arguably the main hero overall.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which Jedi saw clones as numbers and numbers only? I know Pong Krell had a big problem with Clones, but there must be others that didn't saw Clones as people.
Answer: Absolutely. In fact, most Jedi saw the clones as numbers, or sub-sentient. We don’t really get to see “average Jedi” though. So, it’s hard to tell. We see people like Anakin, Yoda (see s1 ep1), Ahsoka, Obi-Wan etc. But the normal Jedi did not care much for their clones. Most people in general certainly did not, as we can see in the Bad Batch. Pong Krell was actually quite esteemed for his victories, even though people knew he had extremely high casualty numbers. At least the Jedi who did respect their clones respected them a lot. In my opinion, Plo Koon loved his clones enough for 50 generals. The Wolf Pack’s (104th battalion’s) gunships had “Plo’s bros” written on them, which I think is really cool.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why is it said that Darth Vader/Anakin Skywalker brought balance to the Force in RotJ if he killed the last Sith, and for there to be balance there should be both Light and Dark/Jedi and Sith (theoretically)?
Answer: It would sound like it! But you have to know what it means to be a Sith, and what it means to be a Jedi. The Jedi are agents of balance. They fight to have the Force in its natural state (good Jedi do, at least) But Sith only serve themselves. They are the unbalance. Sith want all the power to themselves and twist the Force. Otherwise, if we look at another part of the Canon where the Sides must mix for there to be balance - because there most certainly is that part - then the Jedi and Sith are irrelevant. The fighting is the balance, the waves must come and go. Even though it is redundant in a few cases.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which Star Wars faction is your favorite and why?
Answer: The Galactic Republic of course! Its grand army (the clone army) is one of the coolest in all of fiction! They are part of one of the best plots in Star Wars in my opinion. Plus, they are powerful, advanced, they have heart, and they look really cool.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How much damage could the Rebel Alliance do if it managed to get the remaining CIS subjugator class starships (assuming they were still around)?
Answer: They would absolutely help. But less than it seems. The Rebels had one main problem throughout the Age of Rebellion. Lack of members… is how I’ll put it. The Rebels needed hit-and-run tactics, and it worked out pretty well. Fortunately. But they did not really have much choice. This thing would not really work with hit-and-run at all. The Empire had more than enough power to take out a force of ships like that. It’s like the Empire’s an angry human and the Rebels are a bunch of mosquitos. They’re far harder to hit than a pecking bird. Even though a bird’s bigger and can do more damage, it does not compare to a punch or mega-slap from a human. The bird would probably just end up getting hit. While the mosquitos could most likely cause some real misery and live to haunt another day. The inevitable event of losing those ships would cost the Rebels men they could not afford. And what the Rebels had ended up being just enough.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is beskar and why do Mandalorians need it to make their armor?
Answer: Beskar is the metal of Mandalore! It is only found on the planet of the Mandalorians (naturally) And it is very important to them. The mineral is a very big part of their culture and the Mandalorian people believe all Beskar belongs to them. And the most iconic part of their culture relates to their Beskar armor. No Mandalorian armor is truly Mandalorian or traditional if it lacks any beskar. But it can be an alloy. Beskar is the strongest of all Star Wars metals, but it’s also incredibly rare. I’d say there isn’t enough to go around for every Mandalorian to actually have pure Beskar armor. So, most sets just have a little bit of Beskar for their culture.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In your opinion, what makes the original Star Wars movies better than the sequels, prequels, and spin-offs?
Answer: I have two answers for you. #1: Nothing. In my opinion, there are Star Wars spinoffs and movies better than the OT movies. Even though I love them. But here’s what I think the OT does better and why one might prefer the OT to anything else Star Wars has to offer: #2 The Hero’s Journey. For one. No other piece of Star Wars focusses on one young man who has confliction, reaches the point of no return, faces trials, overcomes the climax and makes it back to celebrate. Well, no piece does it as good a way. Star Wars was a perfect example of the classic storyline/plot we all love. And then in the Empire Strikes Back we get incredible scenes, directing and emotion. As well as a little spice where we see the good guys don’t always win. Which is good, it adds layers to the intensity of the battle between good and evil. And finally, we have an amazing climax with a focus on redemption. One of the best things out there. These are arguably the most “classic” and influential movies of all time.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is it possible to draw power from the light and dark side of the Force simultaneously?
Answer: It sure does sound like it. The Bendu and “Father” mention balance in the Force, and they speak of using both Sides. But I doubt even they would say it’s possible. Because in every Canon, every piece of Force lore I’ve seen, the Sides are always opposite. So, while you can argue they are meant to be used in harmony, and both equally, saying it’s possible to use both at the exact same time is a tough sell. The Dark Side primarily runs on uncontrolled emotion: passion. The Light Side primarily runs on Focus and controlled emotion. It would be paradoxical to use both at once.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is your favourite villain of the prequel trilogy? Personally, I loved General Grevious the most.
Answer: They were all absolute fire in my eyes. In fact, it took me minutes to come up with a ranking! But I’ve decided with this: From the prequels alone, using nothing but the movies: I have to hop on the Grievous bus with you. It is so extremely close, but Dooku needs a bit more depth for me to love him. I needed to go a bit deeper. But with General Grievous the short? Not at all. He was instantly a hit. The absolute beast has on of the coolest designs in all of Star Wars, he has FOUR LIGHTSABERS! (I sound like a casual, but it’s hard to get over how cool they are) And he’s just so unique. The Jedi-hunter who was “fixed” to be a mechanical monster. He is the essence of cool villains. And in Legends, there’s great depth too. As for my very close second, it’s Dooku. From AotC alone, we see an absolutely incredible performance from Christopher - as per usual. And he takes out our two favorite Jedi with an elegant, one-handed form. It was simply an amazing reveal of the mysterious aura that surrounded the antagonist throughout AotC. And the last becomes the first counting extra material. Maul was also awesome like Grievous, but in the Phantom Menace alone, we got half a character… Counting Rebels and The Clone Wars, he became my favorite. But still, with stiff competition (he’s not always number one; my list changes)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What other species in the Star Wars universe are known to use the dark side of the Force?
Answer: I have 2 for you. First, from the Canon, we have the Dathomirians! The females, specifically, are more likely to be Dark Siders. “Nightsisters” are people of a Force-using faction other than the Sith and Jedi. They use the Dark Side, and are particularly adept at Sith Alchemy And as strange as it sounds, the other species of Dark Side users is Sith. They - members of the species - were called Sith before the Sith we know. The “anti-Jedi”, let’s call them, adopted the name Sith from the species. The Sith race had a genetic inclination towards the Dark Side (and being left-handed) (EU only)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which of MCU Iron Man's suits looked the best?
Answer: Personally, I like the one in Civil War: MK 46 Looking good, Tony. I can only describe it as “pure coolness and crisp” I don’t know why “crisp”, it just comes to mind. But it was the most advanced suit that stilled had a classic feel. And that’s the best of both worlds in my mind. I loved the nano-suits, and some days I prefer them, but in terms of looks, I’m pretty consistent on loving Mark 46 the most.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which model of the Iron Man suit does Tony Stark use in Avengers: Infinity War?
Answer: Mark L (50 in roman numerals) It was a huge step up from the last suit we saw. This one was capable of creating anything Stark could dream up. Well, almost. The nanobots’ functionality only goes so far. While any shape can be created, utilities are limited to: (Ignore the quality) And the durability is incredible: Overall, the suit definitely put Tony is the next league.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What was Thanos' ultimate goal in the movies and comics?
Answer: They are two different goals. In the comics, Thanos just wants to obliterate everyone because of his creepy crush of the female embodiment of death (“lady death”, not Hela) In the MCU, he was deeply hurt by seeing struggling people. The MCU Thanos was a genius, a visionary and a man with a strong will. After predicting the fall of his people and seeing them ignore him and face the consequences that could have been avoided, Thanos thought it was in his hands to save the universe. MCU Thanos though he would have to save everyone and be fought every step of the way because the necessary solution was not pleasant. While he’s certainly no real hero, I think he’s an amazing villain with a compelling motive, unlike his comic-book counterpart.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is it possible for Dr. Strange to defeat every villain in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, including Darkseid and Galactus, on his own?
Answer: Only if he’s powered by the green sun of Krypton. Dr. Strange is obviously tied for first place. He only stalemated Dormammu because he felt like dying a few times. If Strange didn’t, he would have destroyed the Dark Dimension. But Darkseid and Galactus are tied with the sorcerer for the first-place trophy. So, he’ll need an amp, and there’s only one amp for the job:

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why does Spider-Man: Far From Home keep talking about replacing Iron Man when none of the other movies in the MCU had the public talk about Iron Man in such high esteem?
Answer: Well, it makes sense they would talk about a hero in higher esteem once he’s dead. But it’s really not like Tony wasn’t popular before. By the time of Homecoming, Iron Man was already a very popular and well-loved hero. Of course, since he had not yet proved he was a hero (by giving his life to save everyone else) he was still a controversial figure, but all the Avengers were. Honestly, despite his history, Tony was one of the less controversial figures on the team. Sadly, I say it’s because he was wrong. The right thing is not always the popular thing:

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Thanos determine that he had won during the fight on Titan?
Answer: What fight do you think he was aiming to win? Thanos didn’t want to kill anyone that he didn’t need to. (In his mind, killing half the population is okay as long as it is random) He didn’t come to fight; he came for the Time Stone. Once he had it, he achieved all he wanted to on Titan. So, Thanos did, in fact, leave with a small victory. After he went to Earth and collected the Mind Stone, his victory was complete.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Are you excited for Star Wars: Outlaws, a game that isn’t about Jedi, Sith or any of that?
Answer: Not particularly. But that is because I don’t generally like RPGs like that. Even Jedi Survivor doesn’t appeal that much to me. And it looks like a good game. As for Outlaws, all that can be said is that there is potential. The main is a blank canvas, she can be as amazing or terrible as the devs wish. A commando droid sidekick has to be cool… right? Personally, I think no Jedi will not hurt at all. In fact, it could appeal more! People who aren't Star Wars fans could see it (not obviously Star Wars and all) and get into Star Wars through it. That’s my optimistic view. But from what I’ve seen, the fans in general are not excited. Will it do well? I think it will do okay, maybe a bit less. In the end, no one knows yet.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Do Sith ever use the term "May the force be with you"?
Answer: Never ever! Well, maybe if they’re being fake. But the Sith don’t believe in being with the Force, they believe in bending the Force to one’s own will. You know what? Sith probably wouldn’t be wishing anyone well at all. I don’t think there is a counterpart.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What does Kessel run in 12 parsecs mean?
Answer: It means great navigation and possibly timing. While a parsec certainly sounds like it measures time, it’s actually a measure of distance! And the Run is a 20-parsec course, so what he did is very impressive. But better yet, it shows that Han takes risks and plays by his own rules.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why do Mandalorians use jetpacks?
Answer: To counter the mobility of Jedi. Fly Obi-Wan, fly! The Mandalorian kit is built around taking down Jedi. They jump high? Let’s fly! They block blaster bolts too good? FIRE! Force pull? rope Grapple! You get the point. The Mandalorians mix copying and countering to become the perfect Jedi hunters. Honestly, they do really well. Taking down a Force sensitive as a non-Force sensitive is really impressive. And the Mandalorians do it quite often, so I’d say they did a pretty good job at this whole “gear-selecting” thing.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Grand Admiral Thrawn higher than Tarkin?
Answer: He should be, he really should be. Simply being in the Empire gives Thrawn bragging rights. You know why? The Empire was very xenophobic. Only humans! But Thrawn was the best of the best. Really, if he was leading any offensive or defensive situation the Empire has been in, the Rebels would have been toast for that said round. His military genius is beyond Tarkin’s and the Emperor’s combined - by a lot too. Other than plain stupidity, there was one reason Tarkin was higher up: he was really good at governmental issues. Tarkin knew how to control and organize the ridiculous number of people under the Galactic Empire. He paid attention to the Outer Rim and enforced law very well throughout the entire galaxy. However, he forgot that there are always people willing to fight for freedom, and that they never give up.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win, Obi-Wan or Jango Fett?
Answer: Jango himself would say Kenobi! Why do you think he was running? Fett was scared the moment he saw Kenobi. I think by the time of AotC, the gap between them wasn’t too substantial; Fett put up an excellent fight, but I don’t think Jango expected to win. As deadly as the bounty hunter was, Kenobi was better. His defense was too great for Fett’s blaster (even with a little help from Boba too) Obi-Wan has this in the bag.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: During the Duel of the Fates, what could Obi-Wan Kenobi have done differently to save Qui-Gon Jinn?
Answer: Calm himself. Like how Qui-Gon did. Jinn meditated through the chaos and revitalized himself through the Force. If Obi-Wan did too, he could have used Force Speed (as seen earlier in the film) And then with an energized Qui-Gon and Kenobi, Maul very well could have fell without taking a Jedi with him. But Obi-Wan couldn’t concentrate, he was distracted and stressed. It would not be in vain though! In the very moment Qui-Gon fell, Obi-Wan decided he would be more focused and calmer for the rest of his life. That he would be more like his master, and that patience was the way to go. We actually can see his style change; in the end of the duel, he is far more reactive and precise, and less aggressive. Honestly, I do not think Obi-Wan tapped into the Dark Side there. Obi-Wan seemed surprisingly composed to me.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win, Maul vs Grand Inquisitor?
Answer: Maul, low difficulty. The Grand Inquisitor is deadly, but Maul is in the next league. Maybe more like the one after that. The former Darth could hold his own against 3 inquisitors and I very much think he could have beat them all The best of them should not be a challenge. He could also match Ahsoka and Obi-Wan (both on multiple occasions) Let’s not forget both Kenobi and Tano could challenge Vader. And I don’t need to explain how superior Vader is to the Inquisitors, right?

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who would win, Plo Koon vs Kanan Jarrus?
Answer: Plo Koon, all while keeping his tea in the cup. I really think Jarrus is underrated, but it’s fair when he loses in these matchups. Plo Koon is one of those legendary Jedi. While handicapped by a broken arm - as a practitioner of Form V - he could beat Ventress. And even Yoda in a practice duel (both from Legends though) But even in the Canon, Plo had enough to put him above Kanan. He could effortlessly blitz Sing (someone who could match S2 Ahsoka) Sadly, we don’t have a lot of Plo Koon screentime, but there are also some statements.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How did Snips become so powerful that she could beat Darth Maul in a duel (Ahsoka vs. Maul)?
Answer: She had a good teacher. The perfect teacher for her, really. She helped Anakin grow in pretty much the best way. Tano was just like him, but younger and less experienced, so when he saw something in her that needed correction, it’s likely he found something in himself too, and then they both grow. Plus, Anakin was a freaking beast. He was a master duelist (easily top five Jedi) and very powerful in the Force. And because Anakin stayed close with Kenobi, she would still have his wisdom every now and then. So, when the apprentice of Anakin Skywalker came to fight in the prime of her life, it makes sense that she’d perform so well. (For hypotheticals, I’d bet on Maul, but I do think his defeat was very reasonable)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What Star Wars shows do you expect 'The Acolyte' to be better than?
Answer: Maybe none. It could very well be the worst SW show Disney made by its release. My reasons for thinking so are: 1 It looks exactly like the sequels In a few ways. A new time-period for the Canon, new characters and yet another “first time a female takes charge in Star Wars” 2 Lore Creators have already shared some of the retcons. The most despicable (in my mind) is that the new Canon Force works like this: “The Force will only protect you if you are balanced” Which - in the context - means using both Sides of the Force equally. And that’s stupid and paradoxical in every interpretation of the Force as far as I’m aware.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can Yoda's tutaminis power be used to absorb force lightning from Siths? What is the exact definition of this power?
Answer: That’s like its main thing! Yoda’s only used it for absorbing and redirecting Force Lightning, in the Canon. But it can do more. The definition is as follows: A Force power that grants its user the ability to absorb, dissipate or redirect energy. So, it can do things like this - if the user is a master at the ability: Shan blocking a lightsaber thrust with her hands through Tutaminis And it can also block blaster bolts! Most forms of energy really.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What exactly is that blue and white headdress on Ahsoka Tano?
Answer: It is part of her. The actual headdress is a small “crown” that hides the fade from face to montrals. Montrals are the peaks on top, the three, less-stiff pieces that fall are Lekku. And both can be found on other species (Twi’Leks have Lekku and Kessurians have Montrals) Lekku are more like hairs, but Montrals are sensory organs too. Back to the actual headpiece though: As far as I’m aware, it has no name. But it’s a traditional piece of clothing almost every Togruta can be seen wearing. Ahsoka has one on for all of her screentime with the exception of one scene from her Disney+ series and a few scenes from Tales of the Jedi, where she is a baby.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is your overall opinion of Ray Park's portrayal of Maul in "Solo: A Star Wars Story"?
Answer: The performance was mind-blowing. How he stood up during those 3 seconds was breathtaking. Peak acting. If I was playing that role, there would be no chance of me acting nearly as well. It made me laugh and cry, very emotional. And how could you forget Sam Writer was voice acting! That was also peak Maul right there. One line that’s so forgettable I must assume it was too legendary to remember. Definitely Maul’s best Canon appearance.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Is Yoda truly the best Jedi ever? If not, who is better than him (Canon only)?
Answer: He could be. It depends on the criteria. He was the best duelist and most powerful, but there are 4 strong contenders: 1: Qui-Gon Jinn He is what all the Jedi should have always been. The Force as his guide, his only guide. If he had to break rules to do what he sensed right, he’d do it in a heartbeat. Not because he was rebellious, but because he was so loyal to what all the Jedi should have been loyal too. The Jedi lost their way, they made many rules when they just needed a judge and some guidelines. But the worst part was that everything became about their way, not the Will of the Force. It became about text for them, they forgot why they had rules and where they came form. 2&3: Obi-Wan Kenobi and Plo Koon Both very close. They were perfect Jedi outside of what was mentioned earlier. Loyalty to the Republic and the Order is what put them below Qui-Gon. If they were a little more tuned into the Force and put it above the Order, they would be the two best Jedi. They are so deeply compassionate for everyone, so level-headed, calm and wise. Not to mention powerful and skilled! Both Jedi Masters developed past most of -if not all- their personal flaws and honed their strengths. They were ideal mentors and guides. (If only Obi-Wan had more time with Qui-Gon before training Anakin) 4: Luke Skywalker He is the hero that sparked the flame of the galaxy’s redemption. By Return of the Jedi, he wasn’t the perfect duelist, nor most powerful Jedi ever. But he had the heart to become such. He wanted to do what he was destined to, and through it was hard, he managed. To put it simply, he had guts. In the way I interpreted RotJ’s ending, you’re meant to think Luke goes on to be the G.O.A.T.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Was Yoda present at Sifo-Dyas' funeral in Star Wars: The Clone Wars (TV series)?
Answer: In The Clone Wars, there was no funeral. Sifo-Dyas died… mysteriously. During the Clone Wars, Plo Koon found the dead Jedi’s lightsaber. And then other Jedi masters worked to find out more. In conclusion, they found Count Dooku was the killer and that he really did not want anyone tracing it back to him.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is your opinion of Padmé Amidala?
Answer: Honestly, “mid”. She’s a good person, strong character. But that’s it. Maybe it’s a lack of depth or development (which is acceptable in many cases when storytelling) but I just don’t find her super interesting or relatable. But she plays a huge role, and she’s a really well-rounded character. It’s quite possible George never meant for her to have depth.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the saddest clone death in the Clone Wars?
Answer: The death of ARC Trooper Fives. First, they get us attached to him by showing us how cool he is (should have known better, attachments are forbidden) And that goes on for a while. We keep seeing him overcome impossible odds, see him be vulnerable, we see his heart. And then, Tup’s chip malfunctions. Fives needs answers. After incredible operations, he manages to uncover Palpatine’s plot! The tension and stakes are so extreme and felt all the way through. If he can share this, the Jedi are saved, Anakin is saved, everyone is rescued from the Emperor! But no one believes him. And he’s drugged to look mad and eventually killed. Palpatine got his greasy little fingers into Anakin’s life too much for Skywalker to believe innocent old Sheev could do anything wrong. Fives was directly attacked by Palpatine, but no one believed him. He died utterly alone, and with him died the Jedi’s only hope.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What are some ways that Star Wars lore has changed throughout the years? (Retcons, additions, etc.)?
Answer: So much has been retconned. 1 Lightsaber Lore Lightsaber color used to be very important.’ If it was green, it showed the user was a consular, if it was blue, it would show the user was a guardian. They showed what roles were played and what was in the hear of the wielder. At one point color was dependent on what angle the Kyber's at! Tilting it would change its “frequency” and color. 2 Palpatine’s Death He canonically died, then it was retconned in Legends, then Legends was retconned, then he was brought back in almost the exact same way in the new Canon. Why can’t the moment of the prophecy have an impact? 3 Vader’s the G.O.A.T.? In the G-Canon, Vader was 80% of what Palpatine was. And Palpatine was the strongest Sith. But in the New Canon, Vader is the most powerful to ever have lived, he just had Stockholm syndrome. … Yeah… 4 Shaak, you good? Shaak Ti died about 4 times. So there. That’s all for now, but I hope you enjoyed!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Which other Marvel superheroes that don't have a movie or series would you like to get one?
Answer: Superheroes? Hmm, I would have to go with: Nova Just becuase he’s cool. The MCU is doing a lot of things in space as it is anyway, so I think they have interesting options with Nova. Last of Xandar Can you see it? And… uhhhh. The Sentry I’m sure he’d be nerfed righ- I mean I’m sure he’ll fit right in.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is an important detail from an MCU movie that most people miss?
Answer: I don’t catch a lot of visual details from the MCU, but I’ve learned of a few: 1 this isn’t actually a detail, it’s my theory on why Thor didn’t go for the head. Personally, I don’t think someone thousands of years old would miss a finishing shot or not think of doing so. I think Thor was aware going for the head could save everyone, but he purposefully aimed for the chest. Because it would hurt Thanos. Like how Star-Lord wanted to hurt Thanos for taking Gamora, Thor wanted to hurt Thanos for taking the last person alive he truly loved - Loki Even when Thor reached Thanos, he could have taken the axe and swinged it, but he chose not to. 2 Ross gives Wanda the Accords This is to make her feel more guilty than she already does. Rhodey was the one best suited to read them and they get passed to him almost immediately. 3 Zemo was part of EKO Scorpion A secret squad that committed war crimes. I guess this was to show his moral compass has long since been deactivated.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why would force lightning not badly burn Luke? It seemed underpowered in the originals. Possibly the line ‘unlimited power’ stuck with me. For Palpatine to ditch his lightsaber I would have thought his replacement would be at least as deadly?
Answer: Force Lightning isn’t meant to kill, it’s meant to hurt. On the level Sidious operated on, it could kill, but in a less efficient way. Now, you may think “but that’s despicable!” And you would be right, it is despicable; welcome to the Dark Side. For Palpatine to ditch his lightsaber I would have thought his replacement would be at least as deadly? The main answer here is that his replacement was not just Force Lightning, it was the Dark Side in him. Force Lightning is just so representative of the Sith philosophy that it’s a big favorite for ‘ol Palpy. Even during the Prequels, Sheev did not really want to fight with lightsabers, he though the Dark Side should be the only weapon the Sith need, but it was handy to have a lightsaber and it mocked the Jedi. But during the reign of the Empire, Palpatine was so secured by his underlings -especially Vader and the red guards- that he could confidently discard his sabers. Nothing could hurt him! …

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why didn't any of the 6 Star Wars movies made by George Lucas include montages of prior events or brief flashbacks at key moments of the plot?
Answer: There were never “prior events”. Not far prior, at least. George Lucas didn’t make the episodes in order. He released episodes 4, 5 and 6 before 1, 2 and 3. And while making episodes 1, 2 and 3, he had not even really planned a before. Not enough to make a story of it yet.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: If Dooku (ROTS) fought Maul (Rebels), who would win, and why?
Answer: This is a very good match up. And it’s very close, but only one can be the winner. In my opinion, Maul wins. I actually had a debate on it, and The God Butcher managed to change my mind: The God Butcher's 1st, My 1st The God Butcher's 2nd, My 2nd The God Butcher's 3rd, My 3rd I believe Dooku is, overall, still Maul’s superior, but if Maul really is not as formidable as Dooku, Maul’s advantageous form would negate the Count’s advantage. But only if Rebels Maul is prime Maul. Which is very debatable. Personally, I could see this being true. Maul showed great feats during Rebels while limited by very little screen time. But Maul would absolutely need to be at least near his peak to overcome RotS Dooku.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What level of power would be necessary for someone to resist being conquered by an empire like the Galactic Empire in Star Wars?
Answer: The power of will. Resisting is as simple as refusing to cooperate. And then there’s the next step of taking a stand against the oppression. Which is a step every last one of the Rebels has taken. Additionally, the power of brains and knowledge could make you invisible. If you were someone like Plo Koon, you could probably go undetected on Coruscant!

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: In addition to Count Dooku, what other Jedi and Sith used the Form 2 style in lightsaber combat?
Answer: Not many duelists focus on Makashi. For Jedi, it’s because the Sith were “extinct” and there was no need to focus on lightsaber-to-lightsaber combat. And Sith aren’t normally intricate in their fighting… When they are, it’s normally not to the extent that they main Form II. But they are some good ones: Ventress The most obvious pick, in my mind. Ventress was trained by Count Dooku and he taught her the style of Makashi. She even had what I would call a unique version of Makashi tailor-made for her duel-wielding. The Grand Inquisitor He’s definitely underrated. It’s fair to say he’s not match for the likes of Vader, but we’re talking about Vader! The best of the best, obviously he won’t compare. But on the main point: he’s a pick that won’t show up often because most people don’t know he uses Form II But when he can often be found using only one blade and elegant strikes, toying with lesser opponents. After them, no one really focuses on Form II, but many have mastered it! Including these four who have mastered all 7 forms: And Cin Drallig, but he’s almost non-existent in the Canon.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Who is the highest ranking clone trooper in the Star Wars universe? Is there anyone ranked higher than Captain Rex?
Answer: Oh yes, there were a lot of clones ranked higher than Rex. There are a few odd “ranks” like commandos, specialists ARC troopers, etcetera, but in general the highest rank was commander. Some famous clone commanders include Cody, Wolffe and Fox (thought infamous may be a better word for the last) Rex was only a captain for most of the time (one rank below commander) And that’s actually because of Ahsoka! There can only be one commander, just as there can only be one general. And since Ahsoka was Anakin’s Padawan and also part of the 501st legion, she took the position of commander, holding Rex back. But he did not seem to mind.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: How do blasters work in the Star Wars universe? What makes them powerful weapons?
Answer: In a word? Gas. Blasters charge gas from carriages with enough for hundreds of shots. The color shows the quality. Green is the most powerful, red is strong, but not as good, and blue is great for taking out non-organics/machines, which is why the clones’ blaster bolts are blue.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Can the Jedi have red lightsabers?
Answer: Yeah. In the Canon, no Jedi keeps a red lightsaber, but some have used red sabers for a little while. But in Legends, red was actually a natural color. Adi Gallia had a red lightsaber which was not bleed. She only switched because of the Sith reappearing. I guess it was something of a philosophy, because few people really conscious of the Sith would mistake a Council member for a one.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Since Dagobah was a dark side planet, what if Mace Windu, Obi-Wan, or any other Jedi were to be exiled on that planet? Would they eventually become corrupted?
Answer: Absolutely not. Not for the Jedi you mentioned; those are three of the most incorruptible Jedi in all of Star Wars. But in most cases, a Dark Side nexus doesn’t actually corrupt Jedi. So, if a Jedi were to fall to the Dark Side there, it wouldn’t be directly caused by the planet’s aura. Yoda knew it was a nexus planet, he actually picked it for that reason. It would hide his incredible presence. He felt safe there, and I think any high-end jedi should be able to also.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why did Captain Rex's phase 1 armor look like phase 2? What kind of armor was it because you don't see it on any other clone?
Answer: It was custom! While phase II armor was made to be better than phase I armor, Rex had some problems with it. He preferred the vision of the old, perhaps because he didn’t mind less peripheral vision. And the material was better in phase I, even though it was less comfortable. Those marks stretching downwards on his helmet are from welding two helmets together.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why is MJ back in Spider-Man Far from Home? I thought she moved away in Spider-Man Homecoming.
Answer: The one who moved wasn’t actually MJ That was Liz Allen. She’s also from comics and has been adapted into other shows. But she’s far less popular than MJ Fun fact: she was actually in No Way Home In some way, at least. Seems like she’s lying for fame… Someone is. I doubt we’ll see more of her in the MCU, I guess she was just meant to be a minor loss for Parker.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: Why do clone troopers and Mandalorians look similar?
Answer: Nice spotting! They look similar because the Kaminoans took inspiration from Mandalorians. And it’s fitting because, if you’ll remember, Jango Fett was a Mandalorian. He was the person the Grand Army of the Republic was cloned off of. Plus, it’s a cool design and it was right in front of them. So, it makes sense they went with what was there and already confirmed to work. But it’s not the exact same for multiple reasons. 1 Kaminoans don’t have enough beskar for even ten true Mandalorian set of armor. 2 Clones were not meant to fight Jedi, they were meant for droids. And then after a while, we end up with phase II Which was mainly invented to remedy a lack of vision and poor fitting (Kaminoans don’t exactly make armor for humans often)

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What makes you follow a Quora writer?
Answer: I asked a few of my homies this question, and I conveniently received a request back! It reminded me it's probably a good idea to share my answer because it's pretty unique. The main reason I follow is for connection. I don't care if you are a total noob at writing, if you're a friendly person or even a not-so-friendly person I respect and or admire from a few answers, I'll follow you. And then you have a while to return my respect and make an effort to connect, in which case you get added to the list of homies, or you share with me that you are not willing to return effort and respect, in which case my follow flees to someone else. If you are trying to connect and I'm not, it's probably because you have beliefs you would soon find problematic to me. You don't have to be Christian, but you have to respect my faith and recognize what's unacceptable to me. But yeah, I just look for homies who range from atheists with 1K+ followers to a brother in faith with 60… and later becomes the best SW writer on the platform.

Name: Cade Oosthuizen
Question: What is the best Star Wars Jedi and the best Sith?
Answer: All things considered, the best Sith just has to be Vader. He’s iconic, intimidating, powerful and undeniably one of the best villains of all time. Many fans will argue he is the greatest. And most Star Wars fans will agree he’s the best, even if he’s not the favorite. But for Jedi? We are totally split. Sticking to the most popular Jedi, I’d have to pick Obi-Wan. He’s an ideal Jedi; he lost just as much as Anakin, but never fell. Kenobi stayed strong through the ages and always helped anyone in need if he could. And he was a powerful, wise and skilled master on the Council; what more could you want? But that’s my opinion, Anakin, Luke Yoda Qui-Gon and Plo Koon (underrated ones in bold) are all great picks too. And there are even more than that! Ahsoka’s one example. So, tell me what you think down below and don’t forget to drop a follow and have a great day!
